platform_hints.gitlab: Pull group owners and maintainers. Pull audit event settings. Check project access levels.
platform_hints.1password: Pull vault admin list. Pull activity log settings. Check who can manage vaults and groups.

IAM-08.title: Service Account & Infrastructure Credentials
IAM-08.description: Service accounts, API keys, and infrastructure credentials are registered, authorized, and managed throughout their lifecycle.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization manage service accounts, API keys, or infrastructure credentials with any kind of controls? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have service account and infrastructure credentials practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.command: aws iam get-credential-report --output text --query Content | base64 -d
evidence_commands.shows: Each IAM user's access_key_1_active/access_key_2_active flags and last-rotated dates; look for an active access key with a last-rotated date older than the entity's stated rotation period, or a key still active for a service that has been decommissioned.

The population of IAM identities, including any that function as service accounts; look for a service-style username (e.g., ci-deploy, backup-svc) with no documented owner in the entity's service account inventory.

Account-wide totals for Users and Policies; use alongside the credential report to confirm the count of active service credentials matches the entity's documented inventory count, and look for a discrepancy indicating an unregistered credential.

Whether service-account-style logins are captured under the same enrollment policy as human users, or are excluded entirely; look for a policy scope that silently exempts non-human accounts with no compensating control noted.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: SSWS {api_token}' 'https://{domain}.okta.com/api/v1/users?limit=200' | python3 -c "import sys,json; users=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total users: {len(users)}'); [print(f'{u[\"profile\"][\"email\"]}: {u[\"status\"]}') for u in users[:20]]"
evidence_commands.shows: The directory population, used to confirm no service or integration account is disguised as a normal user profile; look for a non-human-sounding email (e.g., integration@, bot@) without a matching entry in the service account inventory.

The inventory of service accounts in the project with their display names and emails; look for a service account with no description or owner mapping, or one that does not appear in the entity's documented service account inventory.
Key creation dates and types (user-managed versus system-managed) for a given service account; look for a user-managed key older than the entity's stated rotation period with no evidence of rotation.

The inventory of API keys and service credentials tracked in the password manager; look for an item with no owner or tag field populated, or no rotation date, indicating the credential is not formally tracked in the entity's inventory.

collection.question: How do you manage service accounts, API keys, and infrastructure credentials?
follow_ups: Do you have an inventory of service accounts and API keys?
How often are credentials rotated?
Are service accounts scoped to least privilege?

evidence_goals: Pull list of service accounts, API keys, and bot accounts across in-scope systems
Pull credential rotation or expiration settings for service accounts
Pull documentation of each service account's owner and purpose
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Per-system list of service accounts and API keys with owner, purpose, and creation date. Rotation policy or expiration settings. No credentials in source code.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that service accounts are managed without showing the list. Total count without per-account details.
red_flags: Service accounts without documented owner
API keys with no expiration set
Credentials found in source code or config files
Service accounts with admin-level permissions
Unused or stale service accounts still active

platform_hints.github: Pull deploy keys list. Pull GitHub App installations. Pull personal access tokens (if org-managed). Check for secrets in repository scanning alerts.
platform_hints.gitlab: Pull project and group access tokens. Pull deploy tokens. Pull CI/CD variables (check for credentials). Pull service account users.
platform_hints.1password: Pull service account list. Pull vault items tagged as API keys or tokens. Check credential rotation reminders.

IAM-09.title: Access Review Founder Attestation
IAM-09.description: Access reviews in a solo organization anchor on objective system exports rather than self-attestation: {company_name} periodically pulls the user list from each in-scope system, reviews it, remediates unexpected access, and keeps a dated record.
IAM-09.na_trigger: Variant applies only to solo developer organizations

collection.gating_question: As a solo founder, do you periodically pull the list of who has access from each system, check it, and keep a dated record? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have periodic access self-review practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you review access across your systems when you are the only person, and how do you record it?
follow_ups: How often do you run the review?
For each system, do you pull the user list from the system itself or write it from memory?
When you find an account or permission that should not be there, what do you do and how fast?
Where do you keep the dated record of each review?
documents: Identity Provider (Okta / Azure AD / Google Workspace)

evidence_commands.command: gh api orgs/{org}/members --jq '.[].login'; gh api orgs/{org}/outside_collaborators --jq '.[].login'
evidence_commands.shows: The full list of org members and outside collaborators pulled directly from GitHub. Use it as the access export for the code system; every login should be a person you expect to have access.
The full user roster from Google Workspace with admin and suspended flags, pulled from the system. Use it as the access export for identity; every active account and every admin should be expected.

evidence_commands.command: aws iam get-credential-report --output text --query Content | base64 -d
evidence_commands.shows: The IAM credential report listing every AWS user, when they last used credentials, and MFA state, pulled from AWS. Use it as the access export for cloud; every user should be expected and active.
The list of members with access to the Supabase organization, pulled from the system. Use it as the access export for the database platform; every member should be expected.

evidence_goals: Confirm a documented periodic self-review practice that relies on system-generated exports
Confirm reviews actually occurred at the defined cadence with dated records
Confirm each review is anchored on a system pulled user list for every in-scope system
Confirm any unexpected access found in a review was noted and remediated with a dated record
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A short written practice stating the review cadence and that each review starts from a user list pulled from each system. Dated review records across the period, each attaching or referencing the actual system exports reviewed, with any unexpected accounts noted and shown removed.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A single undated attestation that access is fine. A user list typed from memory instead of exported from the system. Review records that skip periods or omit systems.
red_flags: A hand-typed roster offered in place of a system-generated export
Only one review record when the cadence would require several across the period
A system that the entity uses but that never appears in any review
Unexpected accounts noted but no evidence they were removed
Review records with no dates

platform_hints.github: Pull org members and outside collaborators from the API as the access export. A screenshot of the members settings page is an acceptable alternate.
platform_hints.google_workspace: Pull the user roster with admin flags. The admin console users export is an acceptable alternate.
platform_hints.aws: Pull the IAM credential report as the access export; it also surfaces stale credentials and missing MFA.
platform_hints.supabase: Pull the organization members list from the management API or capture the team settings page.

IAM-11.title: Third-Party App & OAuth Integration Review
IAM-11.description: {company_name} maintains an inventory of third-party applications and integrations granted access to core systems through OAuth or API tokens, reviews that access on a defined cadence, and removes integrations that are unused or hold more access than they need.

collection.gating_question: Do you keep track of the third-party apps and integrations that have been granted access to your systems, and review them? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have third-party application and OAuth integration review practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you track and review the third-party apps and integrations connected to your GitHub, Google Workspace, Slack, and other core systems?
follow_ups: Do you have a list of the apps and integrations that have OAuth or API access to your systems?
How often do you review those integrations, and who does it?
When was an unused or over-scoped integration last removed?

evidence_commands.shows: Every GitHub App installed on the organization with the permission scopes it holds and whether it can reach all repositories, revealing over-scoped or forgotten integrations.
Every third-party application each Google Workspace user has authorized through OAuth, with the scopes granted, so unfamiliar or high-scope grants can be identified.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}" "https://slack.com/api/team.integrationLogs?count=200" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(l.get('service_type') or l.get('app_type'), l.get('change_type'), l.get('date')) for l in d.get('logs',[])]"
evidence_commands.shows: The log of Slack app installs and removals with dates, corroborating which integrations were added and whether unused ones were removed.

evidence_goals: Obtain the inventory of third-party apps and integrations with OAuth or API access to core systems
Obtain the granted scopes or permissions for each integration
Obtain records that the inventory was reviewed on a cadence and that unused or over-scoped integrations were removed
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A per-system list of connected apps with owner, purpose, and granted scopes, reconciled against what each system reports as actually installed. Review records with dates. Evidence that removals happened when access was no longer needed.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A claim that integrations are managed with no list, or a list that does not match what GitHub, Google Workspace, or Slack actually report as connected.
red_flags: Integrations with organization-wide or admin scope and no documented purpose
Apps connected long ago that no one recognizes
No cadence for reviewing connected apps
Inventory that omits apps the systems report as installed
Personal accounts authorizing company-data apps outside the inventory

platform_hints.github: Pull the organization installations list and each app's permission set and repository selection. Compare admin-scoped apps against the inventory.
platform_hints.google_workspace: Use the Admin console API tokens report or GAM to list connected OAuth apps and scopes per user. Flag apps with broad Gmail or Drive scopes.
platform_hints.slack: Review the app management page and integration logs for installed apps, requested scopes, and install and removal dates.

NET-01.title: Network Isolation
NET-01.description: System components are isolated by risk and function, production is separated from non-production, and access between segments follows least privilege.

collection.gating_question: Is your production network isolated from development and corporate networks? (Yes/No, even if using cloud VPCs)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have network isolation practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Lists all VPCs with their CIDR ranges and default status; a single default VPC hosting every workload, with no dedicated production VPC, is the tell that production and non-production are not network isolated.

Lists subnets grouped by VPC with their tags; look for subnets explicitly separated by environment (production vs. development or staging) in distinct VPCs rather than one flat subnet layout shared across environments.

Shows the routes each route table allows between VPCs and subnets; a route or peering connection giving the production VPC a direct path to a development or corporate network with no restriction is a network isolation failure.
Lists all VPC networks in the GCP project; production resources sitting in the same default network as development or staging resources, with no dedicated production network, fails isolation.
Lists Azure virtual networks and their address spaces; production and non-production resources provisioned into the same virtual network with no segmentation is a fail.

Shows the deployment protection rules configured on the production GitHub Environment (required reviewers, wait timer, allowed deployment branches); a production environment with no branch policy means any branch, including feature branches, can deploy into the production network, undermining isolation.

collection.question: How is your network segmented to isolate production from other environments?
follow_ups: Do you use VPCs, subnets, or network zones to separate environments?
Is production network isolated from development and corporate networks?
Is your network architecture documented?

evidence_goals: Pull network architecture showing production isolation (VPCs, subnets, network boundaries)
Pull network access rules between environments (production vs non-production)
Pull firewall or security group rules governing inter-segment traffic
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw network config showing: separate VPCs or networks for production, security group or firewall rules restricting cross-environment access, subnet architecture.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Network diagram without underlying config. Statement that environments are separated without showing rules.
red_flags: Production and non-production in the same VPC or network
Overly permissive rules between environments
No network-level separation (application-level only)
Default allow rules between segments

platform_hints.aws: Pull VPC list and CIDR blocks. Check security group rules for cross-VPC traffic. Pull VPC peering connections. Check subnet configurations.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull VPC networks and subnet config. Check firewall rules. Pull VPC network peering connections. Check shared VPC configuration.
platform_hints.azure: Pull virtual networks and subnet config. Check NSG rules. Pull VNet peering connections. Check Azure Firewall rules.
platform_hints.terraform: Pull Terraform state showing network resource definitions. Check environment separation in infrastructure code.

NET-02.title: Boundary Protection
NET-02.description: Boundary protections restrict traffic to required ports, protocols, and sources, with external access points inventoried. Remote access requires strong authentication over encrypted connections.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization use firewalls, security groups, or other boundary protections on your network? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have boundary protection practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Lists every security group and its inbound/outbound rules; a rule allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on a port other than 443 (or 80 redirecting to 443) exposes an unnecessary open ingress point.

Confirms the VPC boundary the security groups and load balancers sit inside; used alongside the security group and load balancer output to check that no resource sits outside a defined network boundary.
Shows whether each load balancer is internet-facing or internal; a database or admin-only service sitting behind an internet-facing (not internal) load balancer is an exposed boundary.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer {api_token}' 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/{zone_id}/settings' | python3 -c "import sys,json; settings=json.load(sys.stdin)['result']; [print(f'{s[\"id\"]}: {s[\"value\"]}') for s in settings if s['id'] in ['ssl','min_tls_version','always_use_https','waf']]"
evidence_commands.shows: Shows the enforced TLS version, forced HTTPS redirect, and WAF toggle at the edge; a min_tls_version below 1.2, always_use_https off, or waf disabled means the boundary is not enforcing encrypted, filtered access.

Lists active custom firewall/WAF rules on the zone; a zone with no rules beyond Cloudflare's managed defaults, or a rule action set to log instead of block for known bad traffic, indicates thin boundary protection.
Lists ingress and egress firewall rules for the VPC; a rule with a 0.0.0.0/0 source allowed on a non web port such as a database or SSH port is an overly permissive boundary.

Lists active Vercel Firewall rules (rate limiting, IP blocking, managed rulesets) applied to the project; a project with no custom rules beyond Vercel's default DDoS mitigation has minimal boundary protection beyond basic availability defense.

collection.question: What boundary protection do you have in place (firewalls, WAF, intrusion detection)?
follow_ups: Do you use a WAF or DDoS protection?
Are firewall rules reviewed periodically?
Do you have intrusion detection or prevention systems?

evidence_goals: Pull boundary protection configuration (firewalls, WAF, security groups facing internet)
Pull inbound port and protocol rules for internet-facing resources
Pull list of external access points (public IPs, load balancers, API gateways)
Pull remote access configuration (VPN, bastion, MFA requirement)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw firewall or security group rules showing inbound restrictions. List of public endpoints. Remote access config showing MFA and encryption requirements.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that firewalls are in place without showing rules. Network diagram without actual port/protocol config.
red_flags: Inbound rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on non-standard ports
SSH or RDP open to the internet
No WAF on internet-facing applications
Remote access without MFA
Unaccounted public IP addresses

platform_hints.aws: Pull security group rules (inbound). Pull ELB/ALB listener config. Pull WAF web ACL rules. Pull VPN and Direct Connect config. List Elastic IPs.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull firewall rules (ingress). Pull Cloud Armor policies. Pull Cloud VPN config. Pull external IP addresses.
platform_hints.azure: Pull NSG rules (inbound). Pull Azure Firewall rules. Pull WAF policies. Pull VPN Gateway config. List public IPs.
platform_hints.cloudflare: Pull WAF rules. Pull firewall rules. Check bot management settings. Pull access policies for protected applications.

NET-03.title: Physical Access Controls
NET-03.description: Physical access to offices and sensitive areas is restricted to authorized personnel, with visitors logged and access reviewed periodically. For cloud infrastructure, data center security is covered by the provider's controls.
NET-03.na_trigger: Does the entity have physical facilities (office, data center, server room) or physical assets requiring access controls?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have physical office space or data center facilities that need physical access controls? (Yes/No, if fully remote with no office, answer No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have physical access controls practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Do you have physical offices or data centers that require physical access controls?
follow_ups: If remote-only, do you use co-working spaces with physical access considerations?
For offices: are there badge readers, visitor logs, restricted areas?
How is physical access removed when someone leaves?

evidence_goals: Pull physical access control configuration for facilities (badge systems, key card logs)
Pull restricted area access controls for server rooms or network closets
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Badge system config showing access levels and approval workflows. Server room access list with restricted membership. Access log config showing entry/exit recording.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that physical access is controlled without showing config. Office lease agreement instead of access system config.
red_flags: No electronic access control (keys only, no audit trail)
Server room accessible to all employees
No visitor access procedures
Physical access logs not maintained

NET-04.title: Production Platform Hardening Managed Platforms
NET-04.description: Production runs entirely on managed hosting platforms, so the platform itself is the control surface: platform access is restricted, production deployments are gated and isolated from previews, secrets live in the platform's managed store, and endpoints enforce TLS.
NET-04.na_trigger: Variant applies only where production runs entirely on managed platforms

collection.gating_question: Does your production run entirely on managed hosting platforms such as Vercel, Railway, Render, or Fly, with no self managed network or virtual private cloud that you configure? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have managed platform hardening practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: The environment variable keys scoped to the production environment with values masked; confirms production secrets live in the platform managed store and are separated by environment
The issued TLS certificates with their domains and expiry; confirms production custom domains have valid unexpired certificates
The variables defined for the production environment of the named service; confirms production secrets are stored in the platform and scoped to production
The teams the authenticated account belongs to; used with a members export from the team settings to confirm who holds access to the production project

collection.question: How is access to your hosting platform, your production deployments, your secrets, and your domain security controlled on the managed platform?
follow_ups: Who has admin or deploy access to the hosting platform organization, and how are those roles scoped?
How is a deployment promoted to production, and are preview or branch deployments kept away from production data?
Where are production secrets stored, and are they separated from non production environments?
How are TLS certificates for your production domains issued and kept valid?

evidence_goals: Pull the hosting platform members list with each member's role
Pull deployment protection or git integration settings showing production promotion gating and preview isolation
Pull the production environment variable listing with values masked
Pull the TLS certificate listing for production custom domains
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw platform settings showing: members mapped to least privilege roles, production deploys gated to an approved branch or protected environment, secrets scoped to production in the platform store, and valid TLS on every production domain.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A statement that the platform is secure without settings output. A client authored spreadsheet of environment variable names. Screenshots that do not show the environment scope or the certificate validity.
red_flags: Any contributor can deploy directly to production without gating
Preview or branch deployments share production data or secrets
Production secrets are absent from the platform store, implying they live in code
A production domain has an expired or missing certificate
Former personnel still hold platform access

platform_hints.vercel: Pull team members and roles from team settings. Pull deployment protection and production branch settings. Run vercel env ls production for scoped secrets. Run vercel certs ls for domain TLS.
platform_hints.railway: Pull project members and roles. Pull environment list to confirm production is separate from other environments. Run railway variables for the production environment. Pull custom domain settings for TLS.
platform_hints.render: Pull team members and roles. Pull the production service settings and environment groups. Confirm auto deploy branch gating. Pull custom domain and certificate status.
platform_hints.fly: Pull organization members. Run fly secrets list for the production app. Confirm the app serves over HTTPS with force_https enabled.

DAT-01.title: Encryption at Rest & in Transit
DAT-01.description: Data is encrypted at rest with industry-standard encryption for databases and storage, and in transit over TLS 1.2 or higher, with cryptographic keys managed through their lifecycle.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization encrypt data at rest and in transit? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have encryption at rest and in transit practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Enumerates customer-managed KMS keys in the account; if production databases and storage report encryption but no corresponding customer-managed key exists, encryption may rely on undocumented provider defaults rather than a managed key lifecycle.
Shows whether storage encryption is enabled on each database instance and which key protects it; any instance with StorageEncrypted set to false is a direct fail for data at rest.

evidence_commands.command: aws s3api list-buckets --query 'Buckets[*].Name' --output text | while read b; do echo "$b:"; aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket "$b" 2>&1; done
evidence_commands.shows: Shows the default encryption configuration for every S3 bucket; a ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError on any bucket holding production or customer data means that bucket is unencrypted at rest.
Shows the encryption status of every EBS volume, attached or not; any in-use volume with Encrypted set to false is a fail.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer {api_token}' 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/{zone_id}/settings' | python3 -c "import sys,json; settings=json.load(sys.stdin)['result']; [print(f'{s[\"id\"]}: {s[\"value\"]}') for s in settings if s['id'] in ['ssl','min_tls_version','always_use_https']]"
evidence_commands.shows: Shows the enforced minimum TLS version and forced HTTPS setting at the edge; a min_tls_version below 1.2 or always_use_https off means data in transit is not consistently protected.

Shows the KMS key protecting a Cloud SQL instance's disk; an empty result on an instance holding production data means it lacks a customer-managed encryption key, warranting a check of what encryption (if any) actually protects that disk.
Shows the encryption services and key source configured on the storage account; a service such as blob or file with enabled set to false is unencrypted at rest.

collection.question: Is your data encrypted both at rest and in transit?
follow_ups: What encryption standards do you use (AES-256, TLS 1.2+)?
How are encryption keys managed (cloud KMS, HSM)?
Are there any data stores that are NOT encrypted?

evidence_goals: Pull encryption-at-rest configuration for all data stores (databases, object storage, block storage)
Pull encryption-in-transit configuration (TLS settings, certificate config)
Pull encryption algorithm and key length settings
Pull key management configuration (where keys are stored, rotation schedule)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw config per data store showing: encryption enabled, algorithm (AES-256, etc.), key source (KMS, managed, etc.), TLS version enforced. Key rotation schedule if configured.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that encryption is enabled without showing per-system config. Summary without algorithm or key details.
red_flags: Any data store with encryption disabled
TLS version below 1.2 accepted
Encryption keys stored in plaintext or source code
No key rotation configured or scheduled
Self-signed certificates in production

platform_hints.aws: Pull KMS key list and rotation config. Check RDS encryption status. Check S3 bucket encryption. Check EBS volume encryption. Pull ELB/CloudFront TLS policy.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull Cloud KMS key rings and rotation schedule. Check Cloud SQL encryption. Check GCS bucket encryption. Pull Load Balancer SSL policy.
platform_hints.azure: Pull Key Vault config. Check Azure SQL TDE status. Check Storage Account encryption. Pull Application Gateway TLS settings.
platform_hints.stripe: Pull API configuration showing TLS enforcement. Check webhook endpoint encryption settings.
platform_hints.supabase: Pull database encryption settings. Check connection SSL enforcement. Pull storage bucket encryption config.
platform_hints.cloudflare: Pull SSL/TLS mode settings. Check minimum TLS version. Pull certificate configuration.

DAT-02.title: Secure Data & Asset Disposal
DAT-02.description: Data and software are securely wiped or destroyed from physical assets before disposal, return, or repurposing. For cloud resources, storage and data are destroyed per provider procedures.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a process for securely disposing of data or hardware when no longer needed? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have secure data and asset disposal practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you securely dispose of data and retire hardware when it's no longer needed?
follow_ups: Is there a formal process for data disposal?
How is hardware sanitized or destroyed?
Are disposal actions documented?

evidence_goals: Pull the written data and asset disposal procedure covering both hardware retirement and logical data deletion
Pull disposal or destruction records for a sample of retired assets, with asset identification, date, and method
Pull the corroborating destruction evidence such as a certificate of destruction, a data-wipe log, or a disposal vendor receipt
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Disposal log entries naming the asset, the date, and the method used, backed by a certificate of destruction, a wipe log, or a vendor receipt, and where cloud data was retired, evidence that the volumes or snapshots were actually deleted.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A disposal procedure with no completed disposal records behind it, or a verbal statement that old laptops get recycled with nothing showing the drive was wiped or destroyed first.
red_flags: Disposal procedure exists but no disposal has ever been logged
Retired asset has no record that data was wiped or destroyed before it left
Disposal log lacks the method used, so it cannot be confirmed the data was rendered unrecoverable
Devices handed to third parties or resold with no certificate or receipt
Cloud storage or backups retired with no evidence the underlying data was deleted

platform_hints.aws: Where data disposal is logical, pull evidence that volumes, snapshots, or buckets were deleted, such as the deletion record or the absence of the resource in a current listing.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull evidence that disks, snapshots, or storage buckets holding retired data were deleted.

DAT-03.title: Data Retention & Deletion
DAT-03.description: {company_name} defines retention periods aligned with contractual and regulatory requirements, deleting or anonymizing data when they expire or on valid deletion requests. Removable media is protected.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a data retention policy or process for deleting data after a defined period? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data retention and deletion practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Shows the configured lifecycle rules (expiration actions, prefixes, and day counts) on a bucket; a bucket holding data subject to a defined retention period with no lifecycle rule at all means objects persist indefinitely with no enforced deletion.

Shows the automated backup retention period in days for each database instance; a BackupRetentionPeriod of 0 means backups are not retained at all, and a period materially longer than the entity's documented retention schedule is itself a gap against the stated policy.

Shows the retention period set on each CloudWatch log group; a retentionInDays value of null (never expire) or one exceeding the documented retention schedule means logs are kept longer than policy allows.
Shows whether Time to Live auto-expiration is enabled on a table holding time-limited data; a TimeToLiveStatus of DISABLED on such a table means expired records are never automatically purged.

Shows the retention period configured on each Cloud Logging bucket; a retentionDays value left at the provider default and never aligned to the entity's documented schedule, whether too short for required records or indefinitely long for data due for deletion, is a gap.

Shows the lifecycle rules in an AWS Backup plan, including the delete-after day count; a plan with no delete-after rule means backups accumulate indefinitely instead of being purged per the retention schedule.

collection.question: Do you have data retention and deletion policies?
follow_ups: Are retention periods defined for different data types?
Is deletion automated or manual?
How do you handle customer data deletion requests?

evidence_goals: Pull removable media and endpoint device protection configuration
Pull data deletion or sanitization configuration for end-of-life devices
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing removable media restrictions (USB blocking, encryption requirement). Device decommissioning process config (wipe, destroy, certificate).
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Policy document about media handling without showing enforcement config.
red_flags: No restrictions on removable media
No device sanitization process for decommissioned equipment
USB ports unrestricted on production endpoints

DAT-04.title: Production Data in Non-Production Environments
DAT-04.description: {company_name} governs whether and how production or customer data may be used in development and test environments. Non-production environments are populated with synthetic, masked, or sampled data, and any copying of production data follows the defined rule.

collection.gating_question: Do you have a rule for whether real customer or production data can be used in your development or test environments? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have production data in non-production environment practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you handle production or customer data in your development, staging, and test environments?
follow_ups: Is real customer data ever copied into development or test environments?
How are non-production databases populated (seed scripts, masked dumps, sampled subsets)?
If production data is used for testing, is it masked or anonymized first, and who approves that?

evidence_commands.command: gh search code --owner {org} "faker OR factory OR synthetic" --json repository,path -L 30
evidence_commands.shows: Where synthetic or fabricated data is generated for development and test environments, supporting that non-production data is created rather than copied from production. Look for seed or factory scripts producing fake records.

Whether any development or staging database snapshots were sourced from a production database instance. A non-production snapshot cloned from a production source is a red flag for raw production data outside production.

evidence_goals: Obtain the documented rule for using production or customer data in non-production environments
Obtain how non-production databases are populated (seed scripts, masking config, or sampled subsets)
Obtain evidence the rule holds over the period (an attestation of no-copy practice, or masking applied to any copies)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A written rule prohibiting raw production data in dev and test, or permitting it only after masking with named approval. Seed or data-generation scripts that fabricate synthetic records. Where copies occur, a masking or anonymization step visible before the data lands in non-production.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A verbal claim that developers do not use real data with no rule and no seed mechanism. Production database dumps restored directly into a staging or local environment with no masking.
red_flags: Development or staging databases restored from production snapshots
Real customer records visible in a test or local environment
No masking step for any permitted production-data copy
No documented rule and no synthetic seed mechanism

platform_hints.aws: Check RDS snapshot lineage for non-production instances cloned from production. Review whether staging restores point at production backups.
platform_hints.supabase: Check whether the staging or branch database is seeded from scripts or cloned from the production project. Review branching configuration.
platform_hints.github: Look for seed, factory, or fixtures scripts that generate synthetic data. Check for any committed production data dumps in the repository.

DAT-05.title: Data Retention & Deletion Execution
DAT-05.description: {company_name} defines retention periods for its classes of customer data and executes deletion accordingly, so that account deletion removes the associated data and backups age out per the configured lifecycle.

collection.gating_question: Do you have defined retention periods for customer data and a way to delete it when it is no longer needed? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data retention and deletion execution practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How long do you retain customer data, and how is it deleted when a customer leaves or requests deletion?
follow_ups: Are retention periods defined for your different classes of customer data?
What happens to a customer's data when their account is deleted?
How do backups age out, and over what period?

evidence_commands.shows: The object expiration and transition rules on the storage bucket, confirming stored data and backups age out automatically per a configured retention period.
The automated backup retention window in days for each database, confirming backups are not retained indefinitely.

evidence_goals: Obtain the defined retention periods for the classes of customer data
Obtain the backup and storage lifecycle configuration showing data ages out
Obtain an executed deletion example showing customer data was removed within the defined window
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A retention schedule by data class. Storage and backup lifecycle settings that expire data automatically. An executed account deletion showing the associated records removed and backups aging out on schedule.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A retention policy on paper with backups configured to retain forever, or a deletion path that removes the account record but leaves associated data in place.
red_flags: Backups with no expiration or infinite retention
Deletion that removes the account but not the associated customer data
No defined retention period for any customer data class
Deleted data still recoverable well past the stated window

platform_hints.aws: Pull S3 lifecycle rules and RDS backup retention. Check whether snapshots are pruned on a schedule.
platform_hints.supabase: Check point-in-time-recovery retention and any storage lifecycle settings. Review the account deletion path for cascade behavior.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull bucket lifecycle rules and Cloud SQL backup retention settings.

END-01.title: Endpoint Protection
END-01.description: Managed endpoints and servers run anti-malware or endpoint detection and response protection, with disk encryption, screen lock, and automatic updates enforced. Detected threats are investigated and remediated.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization use endpoint protection (antivirus, EDR, or endpoint detection) on employee devices? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have endpoint protection practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://api.crowdstrike.com/oauth2/token' -d 'client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; t=json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token']; import urllib.request as r; req=r.Request('https://api.crowdstrike.com/devices/queries/devices/v1?limit=5', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {t}'}); print(r.urlopen(req).read().decode())"
evidence_commands.shows: Returns a sample of devices enrolled in CrowdStrike Falcon; an empty result, or a company-owned device roster larger than the device count returned, means endpoint detection is not deployed across all managed devices.
Returns a sample of agents enrolled in SentinelOne; a device known to be company issued that does not appear in this list is running without endpoint protection.

Lists devices enrolled in Google Workspace endpoint management with their screen lock and encryption status; a device with devicePasswordStatus off or encryptionStatus not encrypted fails disk encryption or screen lock enforcement for that device.

collection.question: Do you use endpoint protection (EDR/antivirus) or mobile device management (MDM) on company devices?
follow_ups: What tool do you use and what percentage of devices are enrolled?
Are policies enforced (disk encryption, screen lock, auto-updates)?
How do you handle personal devices (BYOD)?

evidence_goals: Pull endpoint protection deployment status showing coverage across managed devices
Pull disk encryption enforcement configuration
Pull screen lock enforcement settings
Pull OS and software update enforcement configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Device list showing protection agent installed per device. Encryption enforcement config (FileVault, BitLocker). Screen lock timeout settings. Auto-update enforcement policy.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that endpoint protection is deployed without showing coverage. Product marketing info instead of actual device config.
red_flags: Devices without protection agent installed
Disk encryption not enforced (optional)
Screen lock timeout over 15 minutes or not set
Auto-updates disabled or deferred indefinitely
Unmanaged devices accessing production

platform_hints.crowdstrike: Pull device count and agent status. Pull prevention policy settings. Pull response policy config.
platform_hints.jamf: Pull device inventory with FileVault status. Pull configuration profiles for screen lock and software updates. Pull compliance status per device.
platform_hints.kandji: Pull device list with encryption and agent status. Pull blueprint settings for screen lock and updates. Pull compliance report.
platform_hints.sentinelone: Pull agent status and version across endpoints. Pull policy settings for prevention and detection modes.

END-02.title: Software Installation Controls
END-02.description: Installation and modification of software on production systems is restricted to authorized personnel through access controls and the change management process.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization control what software can be installed on employee devices? (Yes/No, even a policy counts)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have software installation controls practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://api.crowdstrike.com/oauth2/token' -d 'client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; t=json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token']; import urllib.request as r; req=r.Request('https://api.crowdstrike.com/discover/queries/applications/v1?limit=5', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {t}'}); print(r.urlopen(req).read().decode())"
evidence_commands.shows: Returns a sample of the application inventory CrowdStrike Falcon Discover has observed across managed endpoints; unapproved or unrecognized software titles appearing across multiple hosts indicates installation is not restricted to an authorized set.
Returns a sample of installed applications reported by SentinelOne agents; unapproved applications appearing on multiple endpoints indicates a gap in restricting who can install software.

Shows whether GitHub Actions is restricted to selected or verified actions for the organization; a response of allowed_actions all means any workflow, including one that installs or modifies software as part of deployment, can run unrestricted.

Shows the branch protection rules on the production branch; the absence of a required pull request review before merge means changes that install or modify software on production systems can ship without independent approval.

collection.question: How do you control what software can be installed on company endpoints?
follow_ups: Are there restrictions on what employees can install?
Is there an approved software list or app store?
Are unauthorized installations detected or blocked?

evidence_goals: Pull software installation restrictions for production systems
Pull list of production admin accounts with justification
Pull removable media usage policy enforcement configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing who can install software on production. Per-user list of production admin accounts with documented need. Removable media restriction settings.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that installation is restricted without showing config. Admin list without justification for each account.
red_flags: All users can install software on production
Large number of production admin accounts
Admin accounts without documented justification
No restrictions on removable media
No distinction between production and endpoint admin access

platform_hints.crowdstrike: Pull USB device control policy. Pull response policy showing containment capabilities.
platform_hints.jamf: Pull restricted software policies. Pull admin account management config. Pull disk mount restrictions.
platform_hints.kandji: Pull app management policies. Pull admin privilege settings. Pull removable media controls.
platform_hints.sentinelone: Pull device control policies. Pull USB and peripheral restriction settings.

END-03.title: Endpoint Protection Founder-Managed Devices
END-03.description: Where {company_name} manages laptops directly without a central device management platform, every device that accesses production is verified individually. Disk encryption, screen lock, and automatic operating system updates are confirmed on each device against a maintained inventory of production-accessing devices.
END-03.na_trigger: Variant applies only where endpoints are managed directly without an MDM platform

collection.gating_question: Do you verify security settings on each laptop by hand rather than through a central device management tool? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have direct device verification practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you confirm that each laptop used to access production has encryption, screen lock, and automatic updates turned on?
follow_ups: How many laptops access production, and do you keep a list of them?
For each laptop, how do you check that disk encryption is on?
How do you confirm screen lock and automatic updates are enabled on each one?
What happens if a new laptop is added or an old one is retired?

evidence_commands.shows: FileVault disk encryption state on a macOS device. Look for the exact line 'FileVault is On'; anything reporting Off or deferred means encryption is not enforced on that device.

evidence_commands.command: defaults read com.apple.screensaver askForPassword; defaults read com.apple.screensaver askForPasswordDelay
evidence_commands.shows: Screen lock settings on a macOS device. askForPassword should return 1 (password required after sleep or screensaver) and askForPasswordDelay should be a small value in seconds; a large delay or 0 for askForPassword means screen lock is effectively off.

evidence_commands.command: sudo softwareupdate --schedule; defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticCheckEnabled AutomaticDownload AutomaticallyInstallMacOSUpdates
evidence_commands.shows: Automatic update configuration on a macOS device. Automatic checking, download, and install flags should read 1 (enabled); a 0 means updates are not applied automatically on that device.

BitLocker disk encryption state on a Windows device. Look for 'Protection Status: Protection On' and 'Percentage Encrypted: 100.0%'; anything less means the drive is not fully encrypted on that device.

evidence_goals: Establish the full population of devices that access production from a maintained inventory
Confirm disk encryption is on for each device in the inventory using per-device command output
Confirm screen lock is enabled for each device in the inventory
Confirm automatic operating system and software updates are enabled for each device in the inventory
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A current list of every laptop that accesses production, tied to a named person. For each listed device, actual command output or a screenshot of that output showing encryption on, screen lock required after a short idle time, and automatic updates enabled. Every device in the inventory has matching evidence.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A spreadsheet typed by the founder asserting that all devices are encrypted, with no command output behind it. Evidence for one device presented as if it covers the whole fleet. An inventory that omits a device known to access production.
red_flags: A self-authored spreadsheet or verbal claim offered in place of actual device command output
Fewer devices with evidence than the number of people who access production
Any device showing encryption off, screen lock disabled, or automatic updates off
Screen lock idle timeout longer than 15 minutes
A device accessing production that does not appear in the inventory

platform_hints.macos: Run the FileVault, screensaver, and software update commands on each Mac and capture the output per-device. Match the count of captured outputs to the device inventory.
platform_hints.windows: Run the BitLocker status command on each Windows device and capture the output per-device. Confirm protection is on and the drive is fully encrypted.
platform_hints.google_workspace: If devices are enrolled in endpoint verification, the admin console device list can corroborate the inventory and encryption state, but per-device command output remains the primary proof.

VUL-01.title: Vulnerability Scanning
VUL-01.description: Vulnerability scans run on a regular schedule and after significant changes, with findings prioritized by severity and remediated within defined timelines. Configuration compliance is monitored.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization run vulnerability scans on your systems or infrastructure? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have vulnerability scanning practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Lists current Amazon Inspector vulnerability findings and their remediation status; findings that stay active and unremediated past the entity's defined severity based timeline is the tell of a scanning program that exists on paper but is not driving actual remediation.

Lists AWS Config rules and whether each in-scope resource is COMPLIANT or NON_COMPLIANT; a NON_COMPLIANT rule with no corresponding remediation activity signals configuration drift the scanning program is not catching.

Lists which EC2 instances, ECR images, and Lambda functions are actively covered by Inspector scanning; any in-scope resource showing a coverage status other than COVERED reveals a blind spot the vulnerability scan never reaches.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'DD-API-KEY: {api_key}' -H 'DD-APPLICATION-KEY: {app_key}' 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/monitor' | python3 -c "import sys,json; monitors=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total monitors: {len(monitors)}'); [print(f'{m[\"name\"]}: {m[\"overall_state\"]}') for m in monitors[:15]]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists configured Datadog monitors and their live state; the absence of any monitor tied to vulnerability or patch status, or monitors stuck in a No Data state, means a scan finding would never surface as an actionable alert.

Lists Snyk-monitored projects with their last test date and open issue counts by severity; a project with a stale last-tested date or open high/critical issues left unaddressed past the defined remediation window is the failing signal.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts --paginate --jq '.[] | {number, state, severity: .security_advisory.severity, created_at}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists Dependabot dependency vulnerability alerts with severity and open/fixed/dismissed state; a growing number of high or critical alerts left open well past the entity's remediation timeline shows the scanning program is not translating into fixes.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts --paginate --jq '.[] | {number, state, severity: .rule.security_severity_level, created_at}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists static application security testing findings and their open/closed state; a 404 (code scanning never enabled) or alerts sitting open past the severity based remediation window shows scanning scope does not actually extend to application code.

collection.question: Do you perform regular vulnerability scans on your infrastructure and applications?
follow_ups: What scanning tool do you use and how often do scans run?
What are your SLAs for remediating critical, high, medium, and low vulnerabilities?
What is your current scan coverage (all production systems, partial)?

evidence_goals: Pull vulnerability scanning scope configuration showing which systems are scanned
Pull scan schedule or frequency settings
Pull most recent scan results or summary (date, findings count, severity breakdown)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Scan config showing all in-scope systems included. Schedule showing regular cadence (weekly, monthly). Recent scan date and high-level results (not asking for full report, just date and severity counts).
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that scanning is done without showing scope or schedule. Vendor marketing page instead of actual scan config.
red_flags: In-scope systems excluded from scan scope
No regular scan schedule (ad-hoc only)
Last scan more than 90 days ago
Critical findings from recent scans with no remediation timeline
Scanning tool not configured for all asset types (infra, containers, code)

platform_hints.crowdstrike: Pull Spotlight vulnerability assessment config. Pull scan scope and schedule. Pull recent assessment summary.
platform_hints.datadog: Pull Cloud Security Posture Management config. Pull vulnerability scan settings. Pull compliance scan results summary.
platform_hints.snyk: Pull monitored project list. Pull test frequency settings. Pull recent test results summary (severity counts). Pull policy config for auto-remediation.

VUL-02.title: Penetration Testing
VUL-02.description: A qualified party performs penetration testing periodically. Findings are documented, prioritized, remediated, and re-tested for critical and high severity issues.

collection.gating_question: Has your organization ever had a penetration test performed? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have penetration testing practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Lists issues tracking penetration test findings and whether each is open or closed with a closure date; a critical or high severity finding still open well past the entity's remediation timeline, or no tracked findings at all despite a pentest having occurred, is the gap.

Lists merged pull requests remediating a tracked finding and their merge dates; the absence of any linked fix for a documented critical or high severity finding is direct evidence the finding was never actually remediated.

Lists currently open critical and high severity issues still present in the codebase; an issue matching a documented penetration test finding that remains open past the re-test window shows the finding was never actually closed out.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories --paginate --jq '.[] | {ghsa_id, state, severity, published_at}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists repository security advisories and their draft/published/closed state; an advisory tied to a penetration test finding that stays in draft or published with no closure well past the retest window is the tell the finding was never fully remediated.

collection.question: Do you conduct penetration testing, and how often?
follow_ups: Is it performed by an external firm or internal team?
What is the scope (external, internal, web app)?
How are findings remediated and re-tested?

evidence_goals: Pull the most recent penetration test report showing the testing firm, test dates, methodology, and scope (external, internal, web application)
Pull the findings section broken down by severity with the specific issues identified
Pull the remediation and re-test records for critical and high severity findings showing they were fixed and verified
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A dated report from a qualified independent party covering an in scope environment, listing findings by severity, plus tickets or a re-test letter proving critical and high findings were remediated and confirmed closed.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A vulnerability scanner export presented as a penetration test, a vendor certificate or marketing page with no findings detail, or a report with open critical findings and no remediation evidence.
red_flags: Report is an automated scan output rather than manual testing by a qualified tester
Most recent test is more than 12 months old
Critical or high findings listed with no remediation date or re-test confirmation
Scope excludes the primary production application or infrastructure
Testing performed by the same team that built the system with no independence

platform_hints.github: Where remediation of findings is tracked, pull the issues or pull requests referencing the pen test findings to confirm fixes shipped.
platform_hints.linear: Pull the issues created from penetration test findings and their status to confirm critical and high items were resolved.
platform_hints.notion: The report and remediation tracker are often stored here; pull the actual report file and the linked remediation log, not a summary page.

VUL-04.title: Dependency & Platform Update Management
VUL-04.description: {company_name} enables automated dependency update and security alerting for production repositories, defines a window for addressing vulnerable dependencies by severity, and remediates flagged advisories within that window.

collection.gating_question: Do you use automated tooling to alert you to vulnerable or outdated software dependencies in your code? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have dependency and platform update management practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you find and fix vulnerable or outdated dependencies in your production code?
follow_ups: What tooling alerts you to vulnerable dependencies (Dependabot, Renovate, npm audit, Snyk)?
Is it enabled on all production repositories?
What is your target window for fixing critical and high severity advisories?

evidence_commands.shows: The Dependabot configuration for the repository, confirming automated dependency and security updates are enabled and which package ecosystems and cadence are covered.
Currently open dependency vulnerability alerts with severity and the date each opened, showing whether critical and high advisories remain outstanding beyond the entity's window.
A sample of resolved dependency alerts with the opened and fixed dates, so remediation time can be measured against the entity's defined window.

evidence_goals: Obtain the automated dependency alerting configuration for production repositories
Obtain the entity's defined remediation window by severity
Obtain a sample of dependency advisories with opened and resolved dates to measure remediation time
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Dependency alerting enabled on all production repositories. A stated window such as critical within a defined number of days. A sample of advisories showing resolution within that window and no long-outstanding critical or high items.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A claim that dependencies are kept current with no configuration shown, or alerting enabled on only some repositories while others are excluded.
red_flags: Production repositories with no dependency alerting enabled
Critical or high advisories open well beyond the stated window
No defined remediation window
Alerts dismissed without a fix or a documented reason

platform_hints.github: Confirm Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled at the org or repo level. Pull open and fixed Dependabot alerts with dates. Renovate config lives in renovate.json.

platform_hints.snyk: Pull the project list and issue list with severity and introduced and resolved dates.

MON-01.title: Security Logging
MON-01.description: Security event logs (authentication, access changes, configuration changes, admin actions, system errors) are collected from in-scope systems. Logs are retained for at least the defined retention period and protected from tampering.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization collect and retain security logs from your systems? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have security logging practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Lists every CloudTrail trail and its multi-region and log-validation configuration; a trail that is not multi-region, has log file validation disabled, or an empty result with no trails at all means events are not actually being captured account-wide.

Returns the account's GuardDuty detector IDs, confirming automated threat detection is provisioned; an empty list means there is no detector generating security events in the first place, regardless of what downstream logging exists.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'DD-API-KEY: {api_key}' -H 'DD-APPLICATION-KEY: {app_key}' 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/monitor' | python3 -c "import sys,json; monitors=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total monitors: {len(monitors)}'); [print(f'{m[\"name\"]}: {m[\"overall_state\"]}') for m in monitors[:15]]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists configured Datadog monitors covering ingested logs; the absence of monitors built on authentication, access-change, or admin-action log sources means the collected logs are never actually reviewed for anything actionable.

Returns whether the named trail is actively logging right now (IsLogging: true/false), not just whether it exists; a trail that is configured but shows IsLogging as false means log collection has silently stopped.

evidence_commands.command: gam report login start -30d end today
evidence_commands.shows: Returns Google Workspace login success and failure events for the last 30 days with timestamps and IP addresses; a report with no failure events captured, or GAM returning an authorization error, means workspace level authentication activity is not being logged at all.

Lists configured Logpush jobs exporting Cloudflare edge and security event logs to a destination; an empty job list, or a job with enabled set to false, means traffic and WAF events at the network edge never reach the entity's log store.

collection.question: What security logging do you have in place across your infrastructure?
follow_ups: Which systems send logs to a central location?
How long are logs retained?
Are logs protected from tampering?

evidence_goals: Pull logging configuration showing which event types are captured
Pull log retention period settings
Pull log storage and protection configuration (immutability, access controls)
Pull centralized logging or SIEM integration config
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw logging config per system showing: what events are logged (auth, access, changes, errors), retention period, where logs are stored, whether logs are protected from tampering.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that logging is enabled without showing what is logged or retention settings. Summary without per-system config.
red_flags: Authentication or access events not logged
Log retention under 90 days
Logs stored without integrity protection
Some in-scope systems not sending logs
Logging disabled or paused on any system

platform_hints.gcp: Pull Cloud Audit Logs configuration. Check Log Router sinks and retention. Pull Security Command Center settings.
platform_hints.azure: Pull Azure Monitor diagnostic settings. Check Log Analytics workspace retention. Pull Microsoft Defender for Cloud status.

platform_hints.sentry: Pull project settings showing event types captured. Check data retention settings. Pull integration list.

MON-02.title: Security Alerting & Event Triage
MON-02.description: Alerts cover anomalous or suspicious activity and are triaged by designated personnel, with events classified by severity and potential incidents escalated into the incident response process.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have security alerts or monitoring that notifies someone when something looks wrong? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have security alerting and event triage practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Confirms at least one CloudTrail trail exists to generate the underlying events an alert could ever be based on; no trails present means there is no event source for the alerting layer to act on.
Confirms GuardDuty is enabled and actively producing findings; an empty detector list means there are no automated threat findings for any alert or triage process to act on.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'DD-API-KEY: {api_key}' -H 'DD-APPLICATION-KEY: {app_key}' 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/monitor' | python3 -c "import sys,json; monitors=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total monitors: {len(monitors)}'); [print(f'{m[\"name\"]}: {m[\"overall_state\"]}') for m in monitors[:15]]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists Datadog monitors with their live alert state (OK, Alert, Warn, No Data) and notification channels; a monitor with no configured notification recipients, or one stuck in No Data, would never actually reach a person for triage.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Token token={api_key}' 'https://api.pagerduty.com/escalation_policies' | python3 -c "import sys,json; policies=json.load(sys.stdin)['escalation_policies']; [print(f'{p[\"name\"]}: {len(p[\"escalation_rules\"])} rules') for p in policies]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists escalation policies and how many escalation rules each has; a policy with zero rules or no on-call schedule attached means a triggered alert has no defined path to a human, an unactioned-alert gap.

Lists currently open (triggered or acknowledged) incidents with their creation timestamps; a build-up of incidents sitting acknowledged for an extended period with no further activity shows alerts are being seen but not actually triaged to resolution.

Lists configured Sentry alert rules and the conditions that trigger them; an organization with zero alert rules configured means application level errors and anomalies never generate an alert for anyone to triage.

collection.question: How do you detect and respond to security events and alerts?
follow_ups: Are alerts configured for critical events (failed logins, privilege escalation, config changes)?
Who responds to alerts (on-call rotation, security team)?
How are events triaged and escalated?

evidence_goals: Pull alert rule configuration showing which threat scenarios trigger alerts
Pull notification routing configuration (who gets alerted for what)
Pull escalation policy or on-call rotation configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw alert rules showing trigger conditions for security events (failed logins, privilege escalation, suspicious activity). Notification routing to responsible personnel. Escalation paths.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that alerting is configured without showing rules. Dashboard view without underlying alert config.
red_flags: No alert rules for authentication failures
Alerts not routed to security-responsible personnel
No escalation for unacknowledged alerts
Alert fatigue indicators (high volume, low action rate)

platform_hints.datadog: Pull monitor list with query definitions. Pull notification channel config (Slack, PagerDuty, email). Pull downtime schedules.
platform_hints.pagerduty: Pull service list with escalation policies. Pull on-call schedules. Pull integration list (what sends alerts here). Pull incident priority definitions.
platform_hints.sentry: Pull alert rules per project. Pull notification settings. Pull issue assignment rules.

MON-03.title: Security Logging Platform-Native
MON-03.description: Security events are captured through the audit logs of the managed platforms in scope rather than a self-operated log platform. Provider logs are enabled, retained for the defined period, protected from tampering, and either reviewed on a cadence or connected to alerting.
MON-03.na_trigger: Variant applies only where production runs entirely on managed platforms

collection.gating_question: Does your production run entirely on managed platforms where you rely on the providers' own audit and activity logs rather than a self operated log or SIEM platform? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have platform native security logging practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Recent authentication provider log events with type and timestamp; confirms the authentication provider retains an audit trail of sign in and administrative events
Account level audit log entries with actor, action, and timestamp; confirms platform audit logging is enabled and queryable
Each log group with its configured retention in days; confirms logs are collected and shows the retention configured against the entity's policy

collection.question: Which provider audit logs do you rely on, how long are they retained, and how are they reviewed or alerted on?
follow_ups: Which providers' audit logs are in scope (hosting platform, managed database, authentication provider)?
How long is each provider set to retain its logs, and what does your policy require?
Can those logs be deleted or altered, and by whom?
Are the logs reviewed on a cadence or routed into an alerting destination?

evidence_goals: Pull the logging configuration for each in scope provider showing audit logging enabled
Pull the retention setting for each provider alongside the entity's documented retention period
Pull the configuration showing who can delete or alter logs
Pull dated review records or the configuration routing logs into alerting
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Provider settings showing audit logging enabled, retention meeting the entity's policy, deletion restricted, and either dated review notes or a routing configuration into an alerting destination.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A claim that logs are collected without provider settings. A client authored description of what is logged. Retention left at a short default with no policy comparison.
red_flags: Audit logging disabled on an in scope provider
Retention below the entity's defined period or at a short default
Logs can be deleted by any user
Logs are enabled but never reviewed and not connected to any alerting

platform_hints.supabase: Pull the log retention setting and the auth logs from the project dashboard. Confirm database and auth activity are captured.
platform_hints.auth0: Run auth0 logs list to confirm the authentication audit trail. Check the log retention window and any log streams configured.
platform_hints.cloudflare: Query the account audit logs API to confirm platform activity logging. Check retention for the plan tier.
platform_hints.aws: Confirm CloudTrail is enabled and check log group retention with aws logs describe-log-groups.

INC-01.title: Incident Response Plan & Training
INC-01.description: {company_name} maintains a documented Incident Response Plan covering roles, severity classification, containment through recovery, and communication including breach response. The plan is reviewed periodically and designated responders are trained.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have an incident response plan or process for handling security incidents? (Yes/No, even informal)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have incident response plan and training practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Token token={api_key}' 'https://api.pagerduty.com/escalation_policies' | python3 -c "import sys,json; policies=json.load(sys.stdin)['escalation_policies']; [print(f'{p[\"name\"]}: {len(p[\"escalation_rules\"])} rules') for p in policies]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists escalation policies and their rule counts, evidence that the roles and escalation paths described in the incident response plan are actually configured in the tool used to execute it; a policy with no members assigned to any of its rules means the documented roles are not actually staffed.

Lists the members of the GitHub team designated for incident response or security; an empty team or a team of one means the personnel roles named in the incident response plan are not actually assigned to real, trained individuals.

collection.question: Do you have a documented incident response plan, and has your team been trained on it?
follow_ups: Who is on the incident response team?
Have you conducted tabletop exercises or simulations?
How often is the IR plan reviewed and updated?
Does the plan cover communication to customers and regulators?

evidence_goals: Pull the incident response plan document showing defined roles, severity classification, and the containment, eradication, recovery, and communication steps including breach notification
Pull the review record or version history showing the plan was reviewed within the last 12 months
Pull records that incident response personnel were designated and trained, such as tabletop exercise notes or training completion
Pull the on call or escalation configuration that routes incidents to the responsible people
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: The actual plan covering the full incident lifecycle and breach communication, a last reviewed date within the last 12 months, and evidence the response team exists and practiced, such as a tabletop exercise summary with participant names and date.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A one paragraph statement that the company will respond to incidents with no roles or severity levels, a plan with no review date, or a claim of training with no attendance or exercise record.
red_flags: Plan does not name the responsible roles or an incident lead
No severity classification or escalation thresholds defined
No breach or customer and regulator communication procedure
Plan has no review date or was last reviewed more than 12 months ago
Team claims training but produces no tabletop notes or completion records

platform_hints.pagerduty: Pull the escalation policies and on call schedules to confirm incidents route to designated responders.
platform_hints.notion: The plan document usually lives here; pull the actual page with version history to confirm the last review date.
platform_hints.google_workspace: Pull the plan file and its revision history from Drive, and any training or tabletop records stored in Docs or the shared drive.
platform_hints.slack: Confirm a dedicated incident channel exists and pull any pinned runbook or tabletop exercise thread.

INC-02.title: Incident Response Execution
INC-02.description: When a security incident occurs, the entity executes its response program: containing the incident, investigating root cause, resolving vulnerabilities, restoring operations, communicating to affected parties, and documenting the response.

collection.gating_question: Has your organization ever responded to a security incident, or does it have a defined process for when one occurs? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have incident response execution practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Token token={api_key}' 'https://api.pagerduty.com/escalation_policies' | python3 -c "import sys,json; policies=json.load(sys.stdin)['escalation_policies']; [print(f'{p[\"name\"]}: {len(p[\"escalation_rules\"])} rules') for p in policies]"
