evidence_commands.shows: Confirms the escalation policies that would route a live incident to a responder are configured with active rules and members; an empty or ruleless policy at the time of an incident means the response process had nowhere to route the alert.

Lists incidents resolved within the period along with their creation and resolution timestamps; incidents with no resolution timestamp, or a resolution time far outside the entity's defined response targets, is evidence the response process was not carried through to closure.

Returns the timeline of actions on a specific incident (acknowledgment, escalation, notes, resolution); a large gap between detection and the first recorded action, or no notes documenting root cause, shows the response was not actually executed as the plan describes.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories --paginate --jq '.[] | {ghsa_id, state, summary, published_at}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists security advisories tied to a code-level incident along with their remediation and publish timeline; an advisory left in draft with no published resolution well after the incident was contained is evidence the root cause and remediation were never actually documented.

collection.question: Have you had any security incidents, and if so, how were they handled?
follow_ups: How are incidents identified and reported internally?
What severity classification do you use?
Are incidents documented with timelines and root causes?
Do you conduct post-mortems and implement improvements?
Have there been any incidents that affected customer data?

evidence_goals: Pull the incident log or register listing incidents over the period with dates and severity
For a sampled incident, pull the full record showing detection time, containment, root cause investigation, resolution, and restoration of operations
Pull the post incident review or post mortem showing lessons learned and follow up actions
Where an incident affected customer data, pull the notification record to affected parties
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: An incident ticket or timeline with timestamps moving from detection through containment, root cause, and recovery, paired with a post mortem that has an owner and dated follow up actions; if there were no incidents, a credible attestation supported by the monitoring and alerting that would have surfaced one.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A bare statement that no incidents occurred with no monitoring to substantiate it, an alert with no evidence of follow through, or a post mortem with no dates, owner, or completed actions.
red_flags: Claim of zero incidents with no logging or alerting that would detect one
Incident record missing root cause or resolution steps
No post incident review for a significant or customer affecting incident
Follow up actions listed but never closed or dated
Customer data was affected but no record of notification to affected parties

platform_hints.pagerduty: Pull the incident history with timestamps and responders to reconstruct the detection and response timeline.
platform_hints.linear: Pull incident labeled issues and their comment history to see containment, root cause, and resolution.
platform_hints.slack: Pull the incident channel history for the sampled incident to see the real time response and handoffs.
platform_hints.notion: Pull the post mortem documents and confirm each has an owner, date, and tracked follow up actions.

INC-04.title: Post-Incident Review & Corrective Actions
INC-04.description: {company_name} conducts a written review after incidents that cross a defined threshold, capturing what happened, the impact, and the corrective actions, and tracks those corrective actions through to completion.

collection.gating_question: After a significant incident, does your organization document a review of what happened and track fixes to completion? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have post-incident review and corrective action practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: After a significant incident, how do you review what happened and track corrective actions until they are done?
follow_ups: What severity or customer impact triggers a written post-incident review?
Where do you record what happened, the impact, and the corrective actions?
How are corrective actions assigned an owner and tracked until they are completed?
Can you point to a recent review and the fixes that came out of it?

evidence_commands.command: gh issue list --label incident --state all --limit 50 --json number,title,state,closedAt,labels
evidence_commands.shows: Lists incident labeled issues with their open or closed state and close date. Look for post-incident items and corrective actions that are tracked and reach a closed state with a date.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' -H 'Authorization: {api_key}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"{ issues(filter:{labels:{name:{eq:\"incident\"}}}){ nodes { identifier title completedAt state { name } } } }"}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists incident labeled issues with their state and completion date. Look for corrective actions that carry an owner and status and move to a completed state.

evidence_goals: Pull the documented criteria that define which incidents require a post-incident review
Pull the written reviews for incidents that crossed the threshold, showing what happened, impact, and corrective actions
Pull the tracker records for corrective actions showing owner, status, and completion dates
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A written threshold for when a review is required, a written review per qualifying incident that names what happened, the impact, and specific corrective actions, and tracker items for those actions that reach a completed state with dates.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A qualifying incident with no written review. A review that skips impact or corrective actions. Corrective actions named in a review but tracked nowhere or left open indefinitely with no follow up.
red_flags: No written criteria for when a post-incident review is required
A qualifying incident occurred with no written review
Reviews omit what happened, impact, or corrective actions
Corrective actions are named but tracked nowhere
Corrective actions sit open indefinitely with no follow up

platform_hints.linear: Pull issues labeled incident or post-incident with their state and completedAt to show corrective actions tracked to done.
platform_hints.github: List incident labeled issues across open and closed states with close dates.
platform_hints.notion: Export the incident review database and the linked action items with owner and status.
platform_hints.jira: Pull the post-incident review issue type and linked corrective action subtasks with resolution dates.

INC-03.title: Incident Response Solo Operator
INC-03.description: As a solo operation with no on-call rotation, {company_name} relies on automated alerting to the founder, provider status notifications, a lightweight incident log, a ready customer communication template, and post-incident notes to detect, respond to, and learn from incidents.
INC-03.na_trigger: Variant applies only to solo developer organizations

collection.gating_question: Do you have a working way to detect and handle incidents, such as alerts that reach you and a place where incidents get recorded? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have solo operator incident response practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: As a solo operator, how do you find out about and handle security incidents or outages when they happen?
follow_ups: How do outage and error alerts reach you, and have you confirmed they actually get through?
Which provider status pages or outage notifications are you subscribed to?
Where do you write down what happened when there is an incident?
Do you keep a ready template for telling customers if an incident affects them?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists the project error alert rules and the notification target of each. Look for at least one active rule that fires on new errors or error spikes and routes to a channel the founder actually reads, such as their email, phone, or a Slack direct message. An empty list means no error alerting is configured.

Lists uptime and health monitors with their notify settings and the mention handles in the message field. Look for monitors that alert on downtime or no data and that notify the founder directly. Confirms outage alerting exists and names who it reaches.

Lists Cloudflare notification policies with their delivery mechanisms (email, webhook, or PagerDuty). Look for enabled policies for origin health or outage events that deliver to the founder. Confirms provider level alerting is wired to a channel the founder monitors.

evidence_goals: Pull the alert or monitor configuration showing that outage and error alerts fire and route to a channel the founder personally reads
Capture proof that at least one alert or test notification was actually received by the founder
Show subscriptions to outage or status notifications for the critical third party providers the product depends on
Show a lightweight incident log with at least one entry or a tabletop entry, and a ready customer communication template
Show post incident notes recording root cause and a follow up action for any incident in the period
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw alert or monitor config showing outage and error rules whose notification target is the founder own email, phone, or direct message, plus a screenshot of a real or test alert the founder received. Confirmation of subscriptions to the status pages of hosting, database, authentication, and payment providers. A simple but real incident log (a spreadsheet, Notion page, or tracker view) with at least one entry or a tabletop entry, a drafted customer notice ready to send, and post incident notes tying each event to a root cause and a follow up.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A verbal claim that alerts are set up without showing the rules or a received alert. Alerts routing only to an inbox the founder never opens. No provider status subscriptions. An incident log that does not exist in any form. No prepared customer notice. Incidents mentioned but never written up.
red_flags: Alerts route only to an unmonitored inbox or a shared address no one watches
No confirmation that any alert or test notification was ever received
No status subscriptions for the critical dependencies the product runs on
Incidents described verbally but with no log entry or notes
No customer communication template prepared before an incident happens

platform_hints.sentry: Pull alert rules per project and their notification actions. Confirm at least one rule fires on new errors or error spikes and routes to the founder email, phone, or direct message.
platform_hints.datadog: Pull the monitor list with notify settings and message handles. Confirm uptime or no data monitors alert on downtime and mention the founder directly.
platform_hints.cloudflare: Pull notification policies and their delivery mechanisms. Confirm enabled origin health or outage policies deliver to a channel the founder monitors.
platform_hints.uptime_monitor: For a standalone uptime service, pull the monitor list and alert contacts and confirm downtime alerts go to the founder phone or email. Pair with a screenshot of a received alert.

CHG-01.title: Change Management Process
CHG-01.description: Production changes follow a defined process of authorization, review, testing, and approval, and remain tracked and traceable. Secure development practices and baseline configurations support the process.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a process for managing code or infrastructure changes (such as pull requests, code reviews, or approval workflows)? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have change management process practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Proves branch protection requires pull request review before merging to the production branch. Look for required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count of at least 1 and enforce_admins.enabled true. Flag a missing required_pull_request_reviews block, which means changes can merge to production with no review at all.

Proves an automated build, test, and deploy pipeline is defined and active. Look for a workflow with state active covering the deploy path. Flag workflows that are all disabled or a repository with none defined, meaning changes ship without an automated pipeline.

Proves each merged production change carries a recorded review decision. Look for reviewDecision of APPROVED on every row. Flag any merged pull request showing null or REVIEW_REQUIRED, meaning it reached production without the required sign-off.

Proves the GitLab equivalent of branch protection is enforced. Look for push_access_levels restricted to maintainers and merge_access_levels requiring approval. Flag any branch left fully open to direct push, meaning anyone can bypass review.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -u {email}:{api_token} 'https://{domain}.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search?jql=project={project_key}%20ORDER%20BY%20updated%20DESC&maxResults=20' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(i['key'], i['fields']['status']['name'], (i['fields']['assignee'] or {}).get('displayName','unassigned')) for i in d['issues']]"
evidence_commands.shows: Proves individual changes are logged as discrete, assigned tickets moving through a workflow status. Look for tickets reaching a terminal status such as Done with an assignee recorded. Flag tickets stuck open with no owner, meaning changes are not tracked to completion.

Proves the production environment has deployment protection rules configured, such as required reviewers before a deploy runs. Look for at least one protection rule attached to the production environment. Flag an empty protection_rules array, meaning any successful pipeline run deploys straight to production with no gate.

collection.question: How do you manage code and infrastructure changes in your development workflow?
follow_ups: Are code reviews required before merging?
Is there automated testing in your CI/CD pipeline?
Do changes require approval before deployment to production?
Are changes tracked in a ticketing system?

evidence_goals: Pull branch protection or merge rules for production branches
Pull change tracking configuration (issue linking, PR requirements)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Branch protection rules showing: required reviews, status checks, no direct pushes to main. PR templates or issue linking requirements. Change history showing traceability.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that changes go through PRs without showing branch protection config. Process document without system enforcement.
red_flags: No branch protection on production branches
Direct pushes to main allowed
No required reviewers
Admin bypass enabled without restrictions

platform_hints.github: Pull branch protection rules for main/production branches. Pull required status checks. Pull PR merge settings (squash, merge, rebase). Check CODEOWNERS file.
platform_hints.gitlab: Pull protected branch settings. Pull merge request approval rules. Pull push rules. Check required pipeline success.
platform_hints.terraform: Pull backend config showing state management. Check if changes go through PR/plan-apply workflow.

CHG-02.title: Emergency Change Process
CHG-02.description: Emergency changes follow a defined expedited process with retroactive documentation, approval, and post-implementation review. Incident-related changes are identified and tracked.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a process for handling emergency or urgent changes that bypass normal review? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have emergency change process practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Proves whether anyone can bypass the standard review requirement, the technical path an emergency change would use. Look for a small, named bypass_allowances list and admin_enforced true. Flag an unrestricted bypass or enforce_admins false, meaning emergency changes could skip review with no record of who did it.

Proves emergency or hotfix changes are labeled and separately identifiable from routine changes. Look for every returned pull request carrying a reviewDecision of APPROVED despite the expedited path. Flag any emergency-labeled pull request with no review decision recorded, meaning the retroactive review the control requires never happened.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs --jq '.workflow_runs[] | select(.event=="workflow_dispatch") | {name, created_at, actor: .actor.login, conclusion}'
evidence_commands.shows: Proves manually triggered deploy runs, used to push an urgent fix outside the normal automated pipeline, are attributable to a named individual and timestamped. Look for a small, expected set of manual runs. Flag a manual run with no corresponding emergency ticket or pull request, meaning an off-process deployment happened with no trace.

Proves whether any user or group is exempted from the merge approval rule on the production branch, the equivalent emergency bypass path on GitLab. Look for a limited, named exemption list. Flag an unrestricted allowed_to_push or allowed_to_merge setting, meaning anyone could deploy an emergency change with no approval trail.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -u {email}:{api_token} 'https://{domain}.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search?jql=project={project_key}%20AND%20labels=emergency%20ORDER%20BY%20created%20DESC&maxResults=20' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(i['key'], i['fields']['status']['name'], i['fields']['created']) for i in d['issues']]"
evidence_commands.shows: Proves emergency changes are logged as a distinguishable, searchable category of ticket with a creation timestamp. Look for every emergency ticket eventually reaching a closed status with a linked post-implementation note. Flag any emergency ticket left open indefinitely, meaning the required retroactive review and closure never happened.

collection.question: How do you handle emergency or hotfix changes that bypass the normal process?
follow_ups: Is there a documented emergency change process?
Are emergency changes reviewed after the fact?
How often do emergency changes occur?

evidence_goals: Pull the documented expedited or hotfix change procedure showing how emergency changes are authorized, documented after the fact, and reviewed once the emergency passes
Pull records of actual emergency changes from the audit period (hotfix pull requests, expedited merges, break-glass deployments) with their retroactive approval and post-implementation review
Pull the linkage between emergency changes and any incidents that triggered them
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A short written expedited-change procedure plus concrete examples of emergency changes from the period, each showing who approved it after the fact and evidence a post-implementation review happened. If no emergency changes occurred in the period, a clear statement to that effect corroborated by the change history.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A claim that emergency changes follow the normal process with nothing distinguishing them, or a claim that they happen with no examples and no way to identify them in the change history.
red_flags: No defined process for expedited changes, so emergencies simply bypass all review
Emergency changes made but never documented or approved after the fact
No post-implementation review of changes that skipped normal approval
Direct pushes to production with no trace of who authorized them
Frequent emergency changes suggesting the normal process is routinely bypassed

platform_hints.github: Search merged pull requests for hotfix or emergency labels or branches. Check for merges that bypassed required reviews (admin override, force merge). Pull the audit log for direct pushes to protected branches.
platform_hints.gitlab: Search merge requests for hotfix or emergency labels. Check merges that bypassed approval rules. Pull audit events for protected branch overrides.
platform_hints.jira: Pull tickets flagged as emergency or incident-linked changes. Check for retroactive approval fields and post-implementation review notes.

CHG-03.title: Environment Separation
CHG-03.description: Separate environments exist for development, staging, and production. Production data is not used in non-production environments without appropriate safeguards.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization separate development, staging, and production environments? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have environment separation practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Proves distinct named deployment environments exist, such as staging and production, each with their own configuration. Look for a production environment with a deployment_branch_policy restricting which branch can deploy to it. Flag a single undifferentiated environment or a production environment deployable from any branch, meaning staging and production are not actually kept apart.

Proves environment variables, and by extension credentials and configuration, are scoped separately per environment rather than shared across preview and production. Look for production-only variables absent from the preview or development listing. Flag identical secrets appearing in both, meaning a non-production environment can reach production resources.

Proves staging and production run on physically separate database projects rather than one shared instance with logical separation only. Look for at least two distinct project references named for their environment. Flag a single project used for both, the condition the control is meant to prevent.

Proves promotion into the production branch is gated on GitLab, the mechanism that enforces environment separation during deployment. Look for the production branch requiring maintainer approval to merge. Flag a protected_branches list where main allows direct push, meaning changes can reach production without passing through a controlled review step.

Proves actual deployment history shows changes flowing through distinct environments over time, not just a config that says so. Look for a pattern of deployments to a staging or preview environment before the corresponding production deployment. Flag any deployment landing directly on production with no preceding non-production deployment of the same change.

collection.question: Are your development, staging, and production environments separate?
follow_ups: Are they in different accounts, VPCs, or clusters?
Does production have different access controls than development?
Is production data ever used in non-production environments?

evidence_goals: Pull environment configuration showing separate development, staging, and production
Pull access controls showing production is more restricted than non-production
Pull configuration showing whether production data can flow to non-production
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing distinct environments with different access levels. Production access restricted to a smaller group. Data flow controls preventing production data in dev.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that environments are separate without showing config. Architecture diagram without access control details.
red_flags: Production and staging sharing the same database or resources
Same access level for all environments
Production data used in development without anonymization
No clear boundary between environments

platform_hints.github: Pull environment protection rules. Pull environment secrets config. Check deployment branch restrictions.
platform_hints.gitlab: Pull environment configuration and protection rules. Pull CI/CD variable scoping (per-environment). Check deployment approvals.
platform_hints.terraform: Pull workspace or state file separation by environment. Check backend config per environment. Pull variable definitions per environment.

CHG-04.title: Secure Development Lifecycle
CHG-04.description: {company_name} incorporates security practices into the software development lifecycle. Secure coding standards, dependency management, and static or dynamic analysis are applied to reduce vulnerabilities introduced through development.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization follow secure development practices (such as code reviews, dependency scanning, or security testing)? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have secure development lifecycle practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts --jq '.[] | select(.state=="open") | {number, severity: .security_advisory.severity, package: .dependency.package.name}'
evidence_commands.shows: Proves dependency vulnerability scanning runs against the codebase and surfaces unresolved findings. Look for open alerts being triaged within a reasonable window relative to severity. Flag open critical or high severity alerts that have sat open for an extended period with no remediation activity, meaning scanning exists but findings are not acted on.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts --jq '.[] | select(.state=="open") | {number, rule: .rule.id, severity: .rule.security_severity_level}'
evidence_commands.shows: Proves static analysis scanning executes on the codebase and identifies unresolved security findings. Look for open findings trending down over time as they are fixed. Flag a code-scanning setup returning zero alerts across its entire history, which alongside a nontrivial commit history suggests scanning was only just enabled or never actually ran against prior code.

Proves code changes are peer reviewed before merge as part of the secure development lifecycle. Look for reviewDecision of APPROVED on every merged pull request. Flag any merged pull request with no review recorded, meaning code reached production without the peer check the lifecycle requires.

Proves the equivalent review gate is enforced for GitLab-hosted repositories. Look for merge_access_levels requiring at least one approval. Flag a branch where any developer can merge without review, defeating the secure development lifecycle's review step.

Proves specific automated checks, such as tests or a security scan, are required to pass before a merge is allowed. Look for a named security or static-analysis check present in the list. Flag an empty list or one containing only a cosmetic check like formatting, meaning secure coding practices are not actually enforced by the pipeline.

collection.question: Do you follow a secure development lifecycle with security checks built in?
follow_ups: Do you use static code analysis (SAST) or dependency scanning?
What tools do you use for code security scanning?
Are security issues from scans tracked and remediated?

evidence_goals: Pull dependency scanning or vulnerability monitoring configuration
Pull static analysis or code scanning configuration (SAST, DAST, linting)
Pull CI pipeline configuration showing security checks
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw config showing automated dependency scanning (Dependabot, Snyk, etc.), static analysis in CI pipeline, and which checks block merges. Actual tool settings.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that security scanning exists without showing config. Tool marketing page instead of actual settings.
red_flags: No dependency scanning configured
Security scans configured but not blocking merges
Critical vulnerabilities in dependency scan results
Scanning disabled for some repositories
No static analysis (SAST) configured

platform_hints.github: Pull Dependabot config. Pull code scanning (CodeQL) alerts and config. Pull required status checks for security scans. Pull GitHub Advanced Security settings.
platform_hints.gitlab: Pull SAST and dependency scanning CI templates. Pull security dashboard config. Pull merge request approval rules for security findings.
platform_hints.snyk: Pull project list and monitoring status. Pull policy config (severity thresholds, auto-fix settings). Pull integration status with source control.

CHG-05.title: Security Architecture Review
CHG-05.description: New system architectures and significant design changes are reviewed for security implications before implementation.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization review the security implications of major architectural changes? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have security architecture review practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Proves architecture or design-review discussions are logged as discrete, trackable items rather than informal conversation with no record. Look for issues reaching a closed state with a linked decision. Flag a known significant design change with no corresponding issue at all, meaning no review was tracked before implementation.

Proves significant design or architecture changes were routed through a review with a recorded decision before merge. Look for reviewDecision of APPROVED on every labeled item. Flag a merged architecture-labeled change with no review decision, meaning it bypassed the review the control requires.

Proves a minimum number of approvals is technically enforced on the repository holding architecture or infrastructure-as-code changes. Look for a value of 1 or greater. Flag a value of 0 or a missing required_pull_request_reviews block, meaning nothing stops an architecture change from merging without any review at all.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer {api_key}' -H 'Notion-Version: 2022-06-28' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://api.notion.com/v1/search -d '{"query": "architecture review"}'
evidence_commands.shows: Proves architecture review documentation exists as a discrete, searchable record in the team's knowledge base rather than only being implied. Look for pages with recent last_edited_time timestamps aligned to known design changes. Flag a search returning no results despite a known recent architecture change, meaning the review was not documented.

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: {api_key}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://api.linear.app/graphql -d '{"query":"{ issues(filter: { labels: { name: { eq: \"architecture-review\" } } }) { nodes { title state { name } createdAt } } }"}'
evidence_commands.shows: Proves architecture review items are tracked to resolution in the team's issue tracker as a defined workflow rather than ad hoc discussion. Look for issues reaching a Done or Completed state. Flag items stuck in an unresolved state indefinitely, meaning reviews are opened but never closed out.

Proves review requirements are enforced consistently at the organization level across every repository, not only on a single repository's branch protection. Look for an active ruleset with enforcement set to active covering the repositories holding architecture-significant code. Flag an enforcement value of disabled or evaluate, meaning the rule is defined but not actually blocking non-compliant changes.

collection.question: How do you review security implications of significant system changes or new features?
follow_ups: Is there a formal security review process for major changes?
Who is involved in security architecture decisions?

evidence_goals: Pull the process or stated expectation that significant new architectures and major design changes receive a security review before implementation
Pull actual records of a security review for a recent significant change (a design document or proposal with a security section, threat model notes, or reviewer comments raised before build)
Pull evidence of who is accountable for security architecture decisions
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: For a recent major change, a design document or proposal that visibly considered security implications before build, with input from whoever owns security decisions. The review does not need a heavyweight board, but there must be a dated artifact showing security was assessed ahead of implementation.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A statement that security is considered without any design document, review comment, or threat model to show it. Architecture diagrams with no security analysis.
red_flags: No design documents or proposals exist for significant changes
Design records exist but none address security implications
Security reviewed only after features shipped, not before
No one identified as accountable for security architecture decisions

platform_hints.notion: Pull design documents, request-for-comment pages, or architecture proposals. Check for a security or risk section and reviewer comments dated before the change shipped.
platform_hints.google_drive: Pull design or architecture documents. Check version history and comments for security review before implementation.
platform_hints.github: Pull pull request discussions or a design-docs repository for major changes. Check for security-focused review comments on significant architectural work.
platform_hints.linear: Pull project or initiative documents for major features. Check for security review notes attached before implementation.

CHG-06.title: Change Control Automated Gates
CHG-06.description: With no second engineer to review changes, {company_name} controls production through automated enforcement gates on the repository and deploy pipeline, and verifies each deployed change after release.
CHG-06.na_trigger: Variant applies only to solo developer organizations

collection.gating_question: Are your production changes controlled by enforced branch protection that blocks direct pushes and requires automated checks to pass before merging? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have automated change control gate practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: As a solo developer, how do automated gates control what reaches your production branch?
follow_ups: Does branch protection prevent pushing directly to your production branch?
Do required status checks have to pass before a change can merge?
Does the protection apply to administrators, or can they bypass it?
After a change deploys, how do you confirm it is working as intended?

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection --jq '{pr_required: (.required_pull_request_reviews != null), required_checks: .required_status_checks.contexts, enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled}'
evidence_commands.shows: Whether the production branch requires a merge to change it, which status checks are required, whether administrator enforcement is on, and whether force pushes are disabled. Look for enforce_admins true and force_pushes false.
The list of status checks that must pass before a merge is allowed and whether branches must be current before merging. Look for at least one required check tied to the CI workflow.

The CI workflows defined in the repository with their names, active or disabled state, and file path. Look for an active workflow whose job names match the required status checks configured on the production branch.
Recent merged changes to the production branch with their descriptions and the pass or fail status of their checks. Look for a description on each merge and passing checks before the merge.
Protected branch settings for the production branch. Look for push access levels set so no role can push directly and merges are the only path to the branch.
Project level merge settings. Look for only_allow_merge_if_pipeline_succeeds set to true, which enforces that the pipeline must pass before a merge request can merge.
Recent merged merge requests with descriptions and merge timestamps. Compare each with its pipeline status to confirm required checks passed before the merge.

evidence_goals: Pull branch protection configuration for the production branch showing direct pushes blocked, force pushes disabled, required status checks, and administrator enforcement
Pull the CI workflow definition that produces the required checks
Pull a sample of merged changes showing descriptions and passing checks
Pull records of verification performed after deployment
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Branch protection on the production branch with direct and force pushes disabled, one or more required status checks that must pass before a merge, an active CI workflow that produces those checks, administrator enforcement enabled, merged changes that each carry a description and passing checks, and post deployment health checks or smoke tests with results.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A verbal statement that the developer is careful, with no branch protection configuration. Protection that administrators can bypass. Merges with no required checks. No evidence of any verification after deployment.
red_flags: Direct pushes to the production branch allowed
Administrator bypass of branch protection enabled
No required status checks before merge
Force pushes permitted on the production branch
No verification of any kind after deployment

platform_hints.github: Pull branch protection for the production branch: confirm required_status_checks is set, enforce_admins is true, allow_force_pushes is false, and a pull request is required to merge. Pull the actions workflows list to confirm an active workflow produces the required checks. Pull recent merged pull requests with body and statusCheckRollup.
platform_hints.gitlab: Pull protected branch settings confirming no one can push directly and only merges reach the branch. Pull the project settings confirming only_allow_merge_if_pipeline_succeeds is true. Pull recent merged merge requests with descriptions and pipeline status.

BCP-01.title: BCP/DR Plan & Testing
BCP-01.description: A documented BCP/DR plan identifies critical systems, recovery objectives, procedures, and responsible personnel. It is tested periodically, with results used to improve the plan and insurance considered for financial impact.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a business continuity or disaster recovery plan? (Yes/No, even if untested)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have bcp/dr plan and testing practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Proves each production database instance has automated backups enabled with a defined retention period and, where applicable, a Multi-AZ standby for failover. Look for BackupRetentionPeriod greater than zero on every listed instance. Flag any instance showing 0, meaning that database has no automated backup despite being covered by the DR plan.

Proves a centralized backup plan exists defining schedule and retention rules referenced by the DR plan. Look for at least one plan whose rules cover the systems named as critical in the DR plan. Flag an empty response, meaning the documented plan has no corresponding technical configuration behind it.

Proves recovery points are actually being generated on the schedule the plan describes, not just configured on paper. Look for a recovery point with a creation date within the expected backup interval. Flag a vault with no recent recovery points, meaning backups referenced by the DR plan are not actually running.

Proves a restore has actually been executed as part of DR testing, which the control requires be done periodically. Look for at least one restore job with a status of COMPLETED within the last 12 months. Flag no restore jobs at all, meaning the plan's periodic test requirement has not been carried out in practice.

Proves backup job failures are configured to alert responsible personnel as named in the DR plan, rather than failures going unnoticed. Look for an SNS topic configured against a backup job failed event. Flag a vault with no notifications configured, meaning a failed backup could go undetected until the moment a restore is actually needed.

collection.question: Do you have a business continuity and disaster recovery plan, and has it been tested?
follow_ups: What are your RTO and RPO targets?
When was the plan last tested?
What type of test was it (tabletop, partial failover, full failover)?
Does the plan cover communication during outages?

evidence_goals: Pull the business continuity and disaster recovery plan document showing critical systems, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, recovery procedures, and the personnel responsible
Pull the most recent test record showing the plan was exercised (tabletop, partial failover, or full failover) with the date, what was tested, the results, and any follow-up improvements
Pull evidence that communication during an outage is addressed in the plan
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A dated plan naming specific critical systems with their recovery time and recovery point objectives and named responsible personnel, paired with a test report from within the last 12 months describing the test type, outcome, and any lessons that fed back into the plan.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A plan with no evidence it was ever tested, a test claimed verbally with no report, or a backup configuration presented as a continuity plan with no recovery objectives or procedures.
red_flags: No written plan, only an informal understanding of recovery
Plan exists but has never been tested
Recovery time and recovery point objectives not defined or not tied to specific systems
Last test older than the audit period with no recent exercise
Test performed but results and improvements not documented

platform_hints.notion: Pull the continuity and disaster recovery plan page and any test writeups. Check the last-edited date and whether a test record from the period exists.
platform_hints.google_drive: Pull the plan document and test reports. Check document dates and revision history for a test within the last 12 months.

BCP-02.title: Data Backup & Recovery Infrastructure
BCP-02.description: Automated backups run on schedule, monitored for success and stored in a geographically separate location, with restoration tested periodically. Environmental threats are mitigated and alternate processing infrastructure is available.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization back up critical data and have the infrastructure to recover from an outage? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data backup and recovery infrastructure practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Proves each production database has automated backups configured on a schedule and, where MultiAZ is true, a synchronously replicated standby available for failover. Look for BackupRetentionPeriod greater than zero on every instance. Flag any instance showing 0, meaning that database is not being backed up at all.

Proves a centralized backup plan exists defining schedule and retention rules, rather than relying on ad hoc or default per-service settings. Look for at least one plan covering the production data stores. Flag an empty response, meaning no automated schedule governs backups.

Proves automated backups, and point in time recovery if enabled, exist for the production Postgres database, including the timestamp of the most recent backup. Look for a most-recent-backup timestamp within the last 24 to 48 hours. Flag a stale or missing timestamp, meaning the database is not actually being backed up on the schedule assumed.

Proves object storage backups replicate to a geographically separate region, satisfying the requirement that backups are stored somewhere physically distinct from the primary system. Look for a destination bucket ARN pointing to a different region than the source. Flag a NoSuchReplicationConfiguration error, meaning backups exist in only one location and offer no protection against a regional outage.

Proves backup copies are actually executing to a separate destination vault or region, not just configured but never run. Look for copy jobs with a state of COMPLETED on a recurring basis. Flag an empty list despite a configured cross-region copy rule, meaning the geographic separation the control requires exists in configuration only.

collection.question: How do you back up your data, and have you tested restoring from backups?
follow_ups: What is your backup frequency and retention?
Are backups stored in a separate region or location?
When was the last time you tested a backup restoration?
Is backup monitoring in place to detect failures?

evidence_goals: Pull backup configuration for all critical data stores (databases, file storage, object storage)
Pull backup schedule and retention settings
Pull backup monitoring or alerting configuration
Pull backup storage location (same region vs cross-region)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw backup config showing: automated schedule, retention period, cross-region storage, success/failure alerting. Per-system backup settings.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that backups exist without showing config. Backup policy document without actual system settings.
red_flags: No automated backup schedule (manual only)
Backups stored in same region as production
No monitoring or alerting on backup failures
Retention period less than 30 days
Some critical data stores not included in backup scope

platform_hints.aws: Pull RDS automated backup config (retention period, multi-AZ). Pull AWS Backup plans and vault config. Check S3 versioning and cross-region replication.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull Cloud SQL backup config. Check GCS versioning and lifecycle policies. Pull Filestore backup schedules.
platform_hints.azure: Pull Azure SQL backup retention and geo-redundancy settings. Check Azure Backup vault policies. Pull Storage Account replication config.
platform_hints.supabase: Pull database backup settings from project configuration. Check point-in-time recovery window. Pull storage bucket replication settings.

BCP-03.title: Backup & Recovery Provider-Managed
BCP-03.description: Production data lives in provider-managed data stores, so backup and recovery rely on the provider's built-in mechanisms: automated backups or point-in-time recovery with defined retention and separate storage, tested restores with dated evidence, and documented restoration steps.
BCP-03.na_trigger: Variant applies only where production data stores are provider-managed

collection.gating_question: Are your production data stores fully provider managed, for example Supabase, Neon, RDS, or Cloud SQL, so that you rely on the provider's backup and point in time recovery rather than running your own backup infrastructure? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have provider managed backup and recovery practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.

evidence_commands.shows: Each managed database instance with its backup retention period in days and multi availability zone flag; confirms automated backups are enabled with retention and resilience
The Neon project settings including the history retention used for point in time recovery; confirms point in time recovery retention is configured
The Cloud SQL backup configuration including whether automated backups and point in time recovery are enabled; confirms the managed backup settings and retention

collection.question: How are your provider managed data stores backed up, when was recovery last tested, and where are the restoration steps documented?
follow_ups: Which data stores are provider managed, and is point in time recovery or automated backup enabled on each?
What retention is configured, and is backup storage in a separate region?
When did you last test restoring from a backup, and is the result documented?
Where are the steps to restore each data store written down?

evidence_goals: Pull the backup or point in time recovery configuration for each provider managed data store, including retention and region
Pull a dated restoration test record showing a successful recovery from a provider managed backup
Pull the written restoration procedure for the managed data stores
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Provider configuration showing point in time recovery or automated backups enabled with retention meeting the entity's requirement and cross region storage, a dated restoration test with scope and outcome, and a written restore runbook.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A statement that the provider handles backups without configuration output. A restoration test with no date or outcome. A client authored description standing in for the provider settings.
red_flags: Backups or point in time recovery disabled on a managed data store
Retention below the entity's defined requirement or at a short default
Backups stored only in the same region as the primary
No restoration test within the last 12 months
No written restoration procedure for the managed data stores

platform_hints.supabase: Pull the point in time recovery and daily backup settings and the retention window from the project dashboard. Confirm the region.
platform_hints.neon: Run neonctl projects get to read the history retention used for point in time recovery. Confirm the region and any read replicas.
platform_hints.aws: Run aws rds describe-db-instances to read backup retention and multi availability zone. Confirm automated backups and any cross region snapshots.
platform_hints.gcp: Run gcloud sql instances describe to read the backup configuration, point in time recovery, and location settings.

VND-01.title: Vendor Risk Management
VND-01.description: {company_name} maintains a vendor management program: vendor inventory with risk tiering, pre-engagement security assessment, contractual security and privacy requirements, periodic reassessment of critical vendors, and procedures for addressing issues and terminating relationships.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a process for evaluating or managing the security of your vendors and third parties? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have vendor risk management practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you assess and manage risks from your vendors and third-party service providers?
follow_ups: Do you maintain a vendor inventory with risk ratings?
How do you assess vendor security (questionnaires, SOC reports, certifications)?
Do contracts include security requirements?
How often are vendors reassessed?

evidence_goals: Pull the vendor inventory or register showing each third party, the data or access it has, and its assigned risk tier
Pull the pre-engagement security assessment evidence for critical vendors (collected audit reports, completed security questionnaires, or review notes)
Pull contract or agreement clauses covering security and privacy requirements for critical vendors
Pull records of periodic reassessment of critical vendors
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A maintained vendor register listing each vendor, what data it handles, and a risk tier, with the assessment artifact on file for critical vendors (an audit report, a completed questionnaire, or a signed data processing agreement) and evidence that critical vendors are re-reviewed at least annually.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A bare list of tool names with no risk rating or assessment on file, or a claim that vendors are vetted with no questionnaires, reports, or contract terms to show it.
red_flags: No vendor inventory, or a list with no risk tiering
Critical vendors with no security assessment on file
Contracts with no security or privacy clauses for vendors handling sensitive data
No reassessment of critical vendors since onboarding
Vendors handling customer data treated the same as low-risk tools

platform_hints.notion: Pull the vendor register or inventory page. Check for risk tiers, notes on data shared, and links to each vendor's assessment.
platform_hints.google_drive: Pull the vendor inventory spreadsheet and the folder of collected vendor audit reports, questionnaires, and data processing agreements.

VND-02.title: Subservice Organization Monitoring
VND-02.description: Vendors whose controls the product depends on are identified, their SOC 2 reports (or equivalent) obtained and reviewed periodically, and the controls they operate documented.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization monitor the security of critical vendors that are part of your service delivery (subservice organizations)? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have subservice organization monitoring practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: For your critical infrastructure vendors (like AWS, GCP, Azure), do you review their SOC 2 reports?
follow_ups: Which vendors provide SOC 2 or equivalent reports?
How do you handle vendors that don't provide audit reports?
Do you document complementary subservice organization controls (CSOCs)?

evidence_goals: Pull the list of vendors whose controls the product depends on (infrastructure, authentication, payments, and similar subservice organizations)
Pull the current audit reports obtained for those vendors covering the relevant period, or the equivalent certification
Pull the review record showing who reviewed each report, when, the report opinion, and any exceptions or complementary user-entity control responsibilities noted
Pull documentation of the controls those vendors operate on the entity's behalf
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: For each critical infrastructure vendor, a current audit report on file covering a period that overlaps the audit period, plus a short review note recording the report opinion and the complementary controls the entity itself is responsible for.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Naming a vendor as certified without the actual report on file, relying on a report whose period has expired, or obtaining reports with no evidence anyone reviewed them or identified the entity's own responsibilities.
red_flags: Critical infrastructure vendors named but no audit report obtained
Audit reports on file but from an expired or non-overlapping period
Reports obtained but no evidence of review
Complementary user-entity controls not identified or acted on
Vendors that do not provide reports with no alternative assessment

platform_hints.aws: Obtain the current audit reports from AWS Artifact. Check the report period covers the audit period and note the complementary user-entity controls listed.
platform_hints.google_drive: Pull the folder of collected vendor audit reports and any review memos. Check report dates and reviewer notes.
platform_hints.notion: Pull the subservice organization list and review notes. Check each vendor has a current report and a recorded review.

VND-04.title: Subprocessor Change Management & Notification
VND-04.description: {company_name} maintains a current, published list of subprocessors, follows a review step before adding a new subprocessor that will handle customer data, and notifies customers of subprocessor changes in line with its commitments.

collection.gating_question: Do you keep a current list of your subprocessors and notify customers when it changes? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have subprocessor change management and notification practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you keep your subprocessor list current, review new subprocessors before they handle customer data, and notify customers of changes?
follow_ups: Where is your subprocessor list published, and how current is it?
What review happens before a new subprocessor starts handling customer data?
How do customers find out when a subprocessor is added or changed?

evidence_commands.shows: That the public subprocessor list page returns a successful response, confirming the current list is published and reachable by customers.
The change history of the subprocessor list with dates, corroborating when subprocessors were added or removed and supporting the notification timeline.

evidence_goals: Obtain the current published subprocessor list
Obtain evidence of the review step performed before a subprocessor was added
Obtain evidence that customers were notified of subprocessor changes per the commitments
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A published subprocessor list that matches the vendors actually processing customer data. A review record for a recently added subprocessor. A customer notification, changelog entry, or subscription mechanism showing changes are communicated as committed.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A subprocessor page that is stale or omits vendors known to process customer data, or additions made with no review and no customer notice.
red_flags: Subprocessor list missing a vendor that processes customer data
New subprocessor onboarded with no review recorded
No mechanism for customers to learn of changes
Commitment to notify customers with no evidence any notice was sent

platform_hints.web: Confirm the public subprocessor page is live and current. Compare the listed vendors against the vendor inventory.
platform_hints.github: If the list lives in a repository, pull its commit history for add and remove dates.
platform_hints.email: Look for the notification or changelog sent to customers, or the subscribe mechanism that delivers change notices.

EVL-01.title: Ongoing Control Monitoring & Evaluation
EVL-01.description: {company_name} monitors the effectiveness of its controls through ongoing activities and periodic evaluations.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization monitor its own security controls on an ongoing basis (not just during audits)? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have ongoing control monitoring and evaluation practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you monitor whether your security controls are working as intended on an ongoing basis?
follow_ups: Do you perform periodic self-assessments or internal audits?
Are automated monitoring tools used?
Have you had external assessments (pen tests, audits) that provide independent evaluation?

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'DD-API-KEY: {api_key}' -H 'DD-APPLICATION-KEY: {app_key}' 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/dashboard' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin)['dashboards']; print(f'Total dashboards: {len(d)}'); [print(f'{x[\"title\"]}: modified {x[\"modified_at\"]}') for x in d[:15]]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists configured monitoring dashboards with their last-modified dates, evidencing that control-health dashboards exist and are actively maintained rather than built once and abandoned; zero dashboards, or dashboards with a stale modified_at, is the tell that monitoring output is not being kept current.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows --jq '.workflows[] | select(.name | test("(?i)monitor|security|scan|audit")) | {name, state, path}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists scheduled workflows tied to security or control monitoring along with their enabled/disabled state, evidencing automated recurring checks rather than manual one-off reviews; no matching workflow, or a matching workflow in a disabled state, is the tell that monitoring is not actually running on a schedule.

Lists unresolved application issues detected over the trailing 90 days with first-seen and last-seen timestamps, evidencing ongoing detection rather than point-in-time review; a large volume of long-unresolved issues with no recent activity is the tell that monitoring output is being generated but not acted on.

evidence_goals: Pull monitoring configuration that produces evidence of ongoing control operation (dashboards, scheduled reports, automated checks)
Pull examples of monitoring output (log summaries, compliance dashboards, control health reports)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing automated monitoring of key controls (access reviews, backup success, vulnerability scan completion). Dashboard or report config that tracks control health over time.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that controls are monitored without showing how. One-time audit results instead of ongoing monitoring config.
red_flags: No ongoing monitoring (only periodic manual checks)
Monitoring exists but no one reviews the output
Key controls not included in monitoring scope

EVL-02.title: Deficiency Tracking & Remediation
EVL-02.description: Control deficiencies are identified, assessed for severity, communicated to responsible parties and leadership, and tracked through remediation to completion.

collection.gating_question: Does your organization track and remediate security deficiencies when they are found? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have deficiency tracking and remediation practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you track and remediate security deficiencies when they're found?
follow_ups: Is there a formal process for logging and tracking deficiencies?
Are deficiencies classified by severity?
Are significant issues reported to management or the governance body?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists tracked deficiencies as issues with an assignee, open/closed state, and creation and closure dates, evidencing that each deficiency has an owner and is tracked to completion; issues with no assignee, or issues open well past a reasonable remediation window with no activity, is the tell of unmanaged remediation.

evidence_goals: Pull the register or tracking system where control deficiencies and security issues are logged
Pull records showing deficiencies classified by severity, assigned to an owner, and tracked from identification through to remediation
Pull evidence that significant deficiencies were communicated to management or the governance body
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A tracked list of security deficiencies where each item shows a severity, an owner, and open and close dates, demonstrating issues are driven to completion, together with evidence that significant issues were escalated to leadership.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A claim that issues are tracked with no register to show it, or a list of open items with no severity, owner, or closure, so nothing demonstrates remediation actually happens.
red_flags: No central place where deficiencies are logged
Deficiencies logged but not classified by severity
Issues opened but never closed or with no owner
No evidence significant deficiencies reach management or the governance body
Remediation tracked informally in chat with no durable record

platform_hints.linear: Pull issues labeled security or compliance. Check for a severity or priority, an assignee, and status through to done. Pull cycle or project history showing closure over time.
platform_hints.jira: Pull the security or deficiency issue project. Check severity fields, assignees, and resolution status. Pull the workflow history showing items moved to done.
platform_hints.github: Pull issues labeled security or vulnerability. Check assignees, labels indicating severity, and closed status with linked remediation.
platform_hints.notion: Pull the issue or risk log. Check each entry has a severity, an owner, and a status, and that closed items show what was done.

AVL-01.title: Capacity Monitoring & Planning
AVL-01.description: {company_name} monitors production system capacity, sets threshold-based alerts, evaluates capacity against current and forecasted demand, and initiates capacity changes when usage approaches defined tolerances.
AVL-01.na_trigger: Is the Availability TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization monitor system capacity and plan for growth? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have capacity monitoring and planning practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you monitor system capacity and plan for growth?
follow_ups: Do you use auto-scaling or manual capacity planning?
Are there alerts for resource utilization thresholds?
How is capacity reviewed and forecasted?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists CloudWatch alarms configured against capacity metrics (CPU, memory, disk, connections) along with each alarm's current state, evidencing threshold-based alerting before exhaustion; zero matching alarms, or alarms stuck in INSUFFICIENT_DATA, is the tell that the alarm exists on paper but is not receiving live metric data.

Lists Cloud Monitoring alerting policies configured for capacity thresholds, evidencing automated notification before resources are exhausted; an empty result means no automated capacity alerting exists even if the underlying metrics are being collected.

Shows current Postgres connection counts by role against the project's max_connections ceiling, evidencing that database capacity is actively monitored; connection counts persistently near the ceiling with no scaling action taken (plan upgrade, pooler reconfiguration) is the tell that the metric is watched but not acted on.

evidence_goals: Pull capacity monitoring configuration for production systems (CPU, memory, disk, network)
Pull alert or threshold configuration for capacity metrics
Pull auto-scaling or capacity expansion configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw monitoring config showing which metrics are tracked, what thresholds trigger alerts, and whether auto-scaling is configured. Actual settings and values.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that monitoring is in place without showing config. Dashboard screenshot without underlying settings.
red_flags: No alerts configured for capacity metrics
Thresholds set unreasonably high (90%+ before alert)
No auto-scaling or manual-only capacity management
Some production systems not covered by monitoring

platform_hints.aws: Pull CloudWatch alarms for EC2/RDS/ECS. Check Auto Scaling group config. Pull RDS storage auto-scaling settings.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull Cloud Monitoring alert policies. Check managed instance group autoscaler config. Pull Cloud SQL storage auto-increase setting.
platform_hints.azure: Pull Azure Monitor alert rules. Check VM Scale Set autoscale settings. Pull Azure SQL elastic pool config.

AVL-02.title: Availability Monitoring & Uptime Response
AVL-02.description: {company_name} monitors the uptime and health of production systems, alerts responsible personnel when availability degrades or an outage is detected, responds to and resolves availability incidents, and communicates system status to customers.
AVL-02.na_trigger: Is the Availability TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization monitor system uptime and respond to outages? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have availability monitoring and uptime response practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you monitor system uptime, get alerted to outages, and communicate status to customers?
follow_ups: What tool runs your uptime or health checks against production?
Who is notified when a service goes down or degrades?
Do you publish a status page or otherwise notify customers during an outage?
When an outage happens, how is it responded to and resolved?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists configured Synthetic uptime and API tests. Look for active, non paused tests that hit production URLs or health endpoints, evidencing continuous uptime or health monitoring.

Lists alert monitors and their current state. Look for monitors that trigger on availability signals such as a failed health check, endpoint downtime, or elevated error rate, not only capacity metrics.
Lists on call escalation policies. Look for at least one active policy that routes alerts to a named responder or on call schedule, so an outage alert actually reaches a person.

evidence_goals: Pull the uptime or health check configuration running against production services
Pull the alert rule configuration that fires on availability degradation or outage, with its notification target
Pull incident records for any availability outages showing response and resolution
Pull the customer facing status channel used to communicate availability
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Raw monitoring config showing active health or uptime checks against production, alert rules that trigger on availability signals and page a real recipient, incident records for past outages with detection and resolution timestamps, and a live status page or equivalent customer channel.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A verbal claim that uptime is watched with no configuration shown. Alerts that record events but notify no one. A status page that does not exist or was never used during a real outage.
red_flags: No uptime or health check configured for production services
Availability alerts route to no active recipient
Outages occurred with no incident record of response or resolution
No customer facing channel communicates availability or outages
Only internal metric dashboards exist with no uptime or health check

platform_hints.datadog: Pull Synthetics tests for uptime and API checks, and Monitors for availability alert rules and their notify targets.
platform_hints.aws: Pull CloudWatch alarms and Route 53 health checks. Check that alarm actions notify an SNS topic or on call integration.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull Cloud Monitoring uptime checks and alert policies. Check notification channels are configured.
platform_hints.pagerduty: Pull escalation policies and on call schedules to show alerts reach a responder.
platform_hints.statuspage: Capture the public status page URL and any historical incident posts.

INT-01.title: Processing Specifications & Requirements
INT-01.description: {company_name} defines what the system is supposed to do (functional requirements), how well it should perform (nonfunctional requirements), and what data is needed to deliver the product or service. Requirements are reviewed when processing changes occur.
INT-01.na_trigger: Is the Processing Integrity TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization document how data processing should work (specifications, requirements)? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have processing specifications and requirements practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Are your system's processing specifications and requirements formally documented?
follow_ups: Do you maintain documentation of how data should be processed?
Are processing specifications reviewed when changes occur?

evidence_goals: Pull the product or system specification describing functional requirements (what the system processes and produces) and nonfunctional requirements (performance, accuracy, and availability targets)
Pull the data dictionary or API schema listing the data inputs required to deliver the product or service, their sources, and expected formats
Pull the version history or review record for the requirements documentation showing it was updated when significant processing changes occurred
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A maintained specification or API schema that states both functional and nonfunctional requirements (performance, accuracy, availability targets) and defines the required data inputs with their sources and formats, backed by a version history showing the document was revised when processing logic changed.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A verbal description or marketing copy of what the system does, with no written functional or nonfunctional requirements, no defined data inputs, and no version history.
red_flags: Requirements exist only as informal chat messages or shared understanding, not a maintained document
No nonfunctional requirements are stated (no performance, accuracy, or availability targets)
Required data inputs and their expected formats are not defined anywhere
The specification has no dates or version history, so periodic review cannot be evidenced
Significant processing changes shipped during the period but the specification was never updated

platform_hints.github: The OpenAPI or Swagger schema, README, or a docs/ folder often holds the spec and data dictionary; commit history on those files evidences review and updates over time.
platform_hints.notion: Product requirements documents or spec pages, with page history showing edits made when processing changed.
platform_hints.linear: Project or epic specs may describe functional requirements; look for linked spec docs rather than one-line tickets.

INT-02.title: Input Validation
INT-02.description: {company_name} defines what valid inputs look like (data types, formats, ranges), validates inputs before processing, rejects or flags invalid inputs, and maintains records of system inputs for traceability.
INT-02.na_trigger: Is the Processing Integrity TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization validate data inputs before processing? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have input validation practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you validate data inputs to ensure they are complete, accurate, and authorized?
follow_ups: Are input validations automated in the application?
How do you handle invalid or unexpected inputs?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists configured WAF and transform rulesets that inspect and reject malformed requests at the edge before they reach the application, evidencing input validation enforcement; a ruleset with zero active rules, or rules set to log only instead of block, is the tell that invalid input is observed but not actually rejected.

Lists application-level validation error events over the trailing 90 days with timestamps and occurrence counts, evidencing that invalid inputs are recorded with source and time rather than silently dropped; zero results despite active production traffic is the tell that validation failures are not being captured at all.

evidence_goals: Pull input validation configuration for user-facing and API inputs
Pull API request logging configuration showing inputs are recorded
Pull error handling configuration for invalid inputs
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing input validation rules (type checking, length limits, allowed values). API logging config capturing request payloads with timestamps. Error handling for rejected inputs.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that inputs are validated without showing config. Code comments instead of running configuration.
red_flags: No input validation on user-facing endpoints
API inputs not logged
Invalid inputs silently accepted (no rejection or flagging)
No rate limiting on input endpoints

platform_hints.stripe: Pull webhook endpoint configuration. Pull API key restrictions (allowed IPs, permissions). Pull event logging config. Pull Radar fraud rules if applicable.

INT-03.title: Processing Accuracy & Completeness
INT-03.description: {company_name} defines how data should be processed (specifications and expected behavior), detects processing errors through automated or manual controls, corrects errors in a timely manner, and maintains records of processing activities.
INT-03.na_trigger: Is the Processing Integrity TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have controls to ensure data is processed accurately and completely? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have processing accuracy and completeness practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you ensure data is processed accurately and completely?
follow_ups: Are there reconciliation or completeness checks?
How are processing errors detected and corrected?
Are processing results verified?

evidence_commands.command: curl -s -H 'DD-API-KEY: {api_key}' -H 'DD-APPLICATION-KEY: {app_key}' 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/monitor?monitor_tags=processing' | python3 -c "import sys,json; m=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total: {len(m)}'); [print(f'{x[\"name\"]}: {x[\"overall_state\"]}') for x in m]"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists monitors tagged to processing or job pipelines with their current alert state, evidencing an active error-detection mechanism for key processing activities; monitors sitting in No Data state is the tell that the pipeline stopped reporting and processing errors would go undetected.

evidence_commands.command: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs --paginate --jq '.workflow_runs[] | select(.name | test("(?i)process|etl|pipeline|reconcile")) | {name, status, conclusion, created_at}'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists recent runs of processing or reconciliation pipelines with their pass/fail outcome and timestamp, evidencing that processing activity is logged for traceability and that failures are visible; repeated failure conclusions with no subsequent successful run is the tell that processing errors are not being corrected.

evidence_goals: Pull error detection or data validation configuration for key processing activities
Pull processing activity logs or audit trail configuration showing traceability
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing automated error detection (checksums, validation rules, reconciliation). Processing logs with timestamps, input/output records, and error flags.
