collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that processing is accurate without showing error detection config. Application code instead of running configuration.
red_flags: No automated error detection for critical processing
Processing logs missing timestamps or source identifiers
No reconciliation between input and output

INT-04.title: Output Controls
INT-04.description: {company_name} protects processing outputs from unauthorized access or modification, distributes outputs only to intended recipients, verifies output completeness and accuracy, and maintains records of output activities.
INT-04.na_trigger: Is the Processing Integrity TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization control how processed data is delivered or output? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have output controls practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you ensure system outputs are complete, accurate, and delivered to the right recipients?
follow_ups: Are outputs validated before delivery?
How is output distribution controlled?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists storage buckets with their public or private flag, evidencing that outputs delivered to users are held in access-controlled storage rather than open to the public; a bucket holding generated output files with public set to true is the tell of an unauthorized-access exposure.

Lists Cloudflare Access applications gating output-delivery endpoints along with their configured identity policies, evidencing that only authenticated, authorized recipients can reach generated outputs; an output-delivery endpoint absent from this list is the tell that it is reachable without authorization.

evidence_goals: Pull access controls on processing outputs (reports, data exports, API responses)
Pull output distribution configuration showing delivery to authorized recipients only
Pull output verification or completeness check configuration
Pull output activity logging configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing access controls on output storage/delivery. Distribution lists or access policies. Verification steps before output delivery. Audit logs of output activities.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that outputs are controlled without showing config. Process description without system enforcement.
red_flags: Outputs accessible to unauthorized users
No verification before output delivery
No logging of who accessed or received outputs
Outputs sent via unencrypted channels

INT-05.title: Data Storage Integrity
INT-05.description: {company_name} protects stored data from unauthorized modification or deletion, ensures data is stored completely and accurately, archives system records per retention requirements, and maintains records of storage activities.
INT-05.na_trigger: Is the Processing Integrity TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization protect the integrity of stored data? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data storage integrity practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you protect the integrity of stored data against unauthorized modification?
follow_ups: Are there checksums or integrity monitoring on critical data?
How are data modifications tracked and audited?

evidence_commands.command: psql {connection_string} -c "SELECT schemaname, tablename, rowsecurity FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public';"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists application tables with row level security enabled or disabled, evidencing that stored data is protected from unauthorized modification at the database layer; any table holding customer data with rowsecurity set to false is the tell of an unprotected table.

Shows the configured backup retention period and deletion protection flag for each database instance, evidencing that stored data is archived and protected against accidental or unauthorized deletion; a retention period of 0 days or DeletionProtection set to false is the tell of a gap.

Shows whether Postgres data page checksums are enabled on the database cluster, evidencing an active integrity check that can detect storage-level corruption; a result of off is the tell that stored data completeness and accuracy are not being verified at the storage layer.

evidence_goals: Pull access controls on stored data (database permissions, storage ACLs)
Pull data integrity check configuration (checksums, replication verification)
Pull data archival and retention configuration
Pull storage activity logging configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Database or storage ACL config showing write access is restricted. Integrity check config (replication lag monitoring, checksum verification). Archival settings with retention periods. Storage access audit logs.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Statement that data is protected without showing access controls. Application-level auth instead of storage-level config.
red_flags: Broad write access to production data stores
No integrity checks on stored data
No archival or retention configuration
Storage access not logged

PRI-01.title: Privacy Notice & Communication
PRI-01.description: {company_name} provides a clearly written privacy notice describing what personal information is collected, why, who it is shared with, and data subjects' rights. The notice is reviewed when practices change, and prior versions are retained.
PRI-01.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization publish a privacy notice that tells people how their personal information is collected, used, and shared? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have privacy notice and communication practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Do you have a privacy notice that explains how you collect, use, and share personal information?
follow_ups: Where is the privacy notice published?
Does it cover all required elements (data types, purposes, retention, rights)?
How are updates communicated to users?

evidence_goals: Pull the published privacy notice at its live URL and confirm it is reachable before or at the point of data collection, such as linked from the signup flow and the site footer
Review the notice for the required elements: types of personal information collected, purposes of use, third-party disclosures, data subject rights, and the entities and activities covered
Pull the version history or archived prior versions of the notice and any record showing changes were communicated to users
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A live, dated privacy notice written in plain language that lists the personal information collected, the purposes, the third parties it is shared with, and data subject rights, backed by a version history or archived prior versions and a record of how changes were announced.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A privacy notice pasted into the submission with no live URL, no date, and no version history, or a notice missing whole required sections such as data subject rights or third-party disclosures.
red_flags: The notice is not linked from the signup flow or is only reachable after an account is created
No date on the notice, or the date is older than 24 months
Missing required sections such as data subject rights, third-party disclosures, or purposes
Boilerplate copied from another company that still names a different entity or product
No archive of prior versions and no evidence users were told when the notice changed

platform_hints.github: If the marketing site is in a repo, the privacy page source and its commit history give both the current notice and a dated version trail.
platform_hints.notion: A public Notion or CMS page may host the notice; export the page and check page history for prior versions.

PRI-02.title: Consent Management
PRI-02.description: {company_name} obtains consent before collecting or using personal information, informing data subjects of their choices. Explicit consent covers sensitive information, cross-border transfers, and any new purposes.
PRI-02.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization collect consent before collecting or processing personal information? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have consent management practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you obtain and manage consent for collecting and using personal information?
follow_ups: Is consent explicit (opt-in) or implicit?
Can users withdraw consent, and how?
Do you maintain records of consent?

evidence_goals: Pull consent collection mechanism configuration (cookie banners, signup forms, consent checkboxes)
Pull separate consent configuration for sensitive data or cross-border transfers
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config of consent mechanism showing it fires before or at data collection. Separate consent flow config for sensitive data categories. Consent records storage config.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Privacy policy document without showing how consent is actually collected in the product. Statement that consent is obtained.
red_flags: No consent mechanism before data collection
Pre-checked consent boxes
No separate consent for sensitive data
No record of consent stored

PRI-03.title: Personal Information Collection
PRI-03.description: {company_name} collects only the personal information described in its privacy notice, through fair and lawful methods and reliable third-party sources. Data subjects are informed when collection goes beyond the original scope.
PRI-03.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have documented practices for how personal information is collected? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have personal information collection practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you control what personal information is collected and ensure it's limited to what's needed?
follow_ups: Do you have a data inventory that identifies what personal data you collect?
Is collection limited to disclosed purposes?
How is implicit collection (cookies, analytics) managed?

evidence_goals: Pull data collection points in the application showing what personal information is collected
Pull comparison configuration between actual collection and privacy notice disclosures
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Data flow or schema showing what personal information fields are collected at each point. Mapping between collected fields and what the privacy notice discloses.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Privacy notice alone without showing actual collection points. Statement that collection matches the notice.
red_flags: Data fields collected that are not mentioned in privacy notice
Hidden data collection (analytics, tracking) not disclosed
Collection scope broader than stated purpose

PRI-04.title: Use & Purpose Limitation
PRI-04.description: {company_name} uses personal information only for the purposes disclosed in its privacy notice or covered by consent, with controls preventing undisclosed use and new consent obtained before any new purpose.
PRI-04.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization limit the use of personal information to the purposes stated in your privacy notice? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have use and purpose limitation practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you ensure personal information is only used for the purposes disclosed to data subjects?
follow_ups: Are there controls preventing use beyond disclosed purposes?
How is data retained and when is it deleted?

evidence_goals: Pull data usage configuration showing how personal information is used in the system
Pull controls or restrictions preventing undisclosed uses of personal data
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config or data flow showing actual uses of personal data mapped against privacy notice purposes. Access controls limiting who can use data for what. Audit log of data access by purpose.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Privacy notice listing permitted uses without showing actual enforcement. Statement that uses align with notice.
red_flags: Personal data used for purposes not in privacy notice
No access controls limiting data use by purpose
Data shared with internal teams beyond stated scope

PRI-05.title: Data Subject Access & Correction Rights
PRI-05.description: Data subjects can access, correct, and update their personal information on authenticated request, with responses inside defined timeframes and denials explained in writing with appeal instructions.
PRI-05.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization allow individuals to access, correct, or delete their personal information? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data subject access and correction rights practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How can data subjects access, correct, or delete their personal information?
follow_ups: Do you have a process for handling data subject access requests (DSARs)?
What is your response timeline?
Can subjects request deletion of their data?

evidence_goals: Pull self-service data access or correction mechanism configuration (account settings, data export)
Pull data subject request handling configuration (intake form, workflow, SLA)
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing self-service data access or correction feature in the product. DSR intake mechanism config with response SLA. Workflow showing how requests are fulfilled.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Policy stating data subjects have rights without showing how they exercise them. No actual mechanism configured.
red_flags: No self-service mechanism for data access or correction
No intake mechanism for data subject requests
No defined SLA for responding to requests

PRI-06.title: Disclosure & Third-Party Management
PRI-06.description: {company_name} discloses personal information only for approved purposes to authorized third parties bound by privacy agreements. Disclosures are recorded, and third parties are assessed for privacy compliance and required to report unauthorized disclosures.
PRI-06.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization control how personal information is disclosed to third parties? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have disclosure and third-party management practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you manage disclosure of personal information to third parties?
follow_ups: Do you have data processing agreements (DPAs) with third parties?
How do you ensure third parties protect the data?
Is disclosure limited to the purposes disclosed to data subjects?

evidence_goals: Pull disclosure tracking configuration (records of who, what, when, to whom)
Pull breach disclosure record-keeping configuration
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Config showing how authorized data disclosures are logged (third-party data sharing records, DPA tracking). Breach incident record config with required fields (date, scope, recipients notified).
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Privacy policy mentioning disclosures without showing tracking mechanism. Statement that breaches are tracked.
red_flags: No tracking of data shared with third parties
No breach disclosure record-keeping
Disclosures happening without records

PRI-07.title: Privacy Breach Notification
PRI-07.description: {company_name} identifies applicable breach reporting requirements, defines notification procedures with timelines and responsible parties, and provides timely notice of breaches to affected data subjects, regulators, and other required recipients.
PRI-07.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a process for notifying affected individuals and authorities when a privacy breach occurs? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have privacy breach notification practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Do you have a process for notifying affected individuals and regulators in case of a privacy breach?
follow_ups: What are your notification timelines?
Does the process cover both individual and regulatory notifications?
How do you determine who needs to be notified?

evidence_goals: Pull the breach notification procedure listing the applicable regulatory and contractual reporting requirements, including statutory deadlines and any customer contract clauses
Pull the procedure section that defines notification timelines, the responsible parties, and the required notification content or templates
For any breaches during the period, pull the notification records showing recipients, dates sent, and content, or obtain written confirmation that no breaches occurred
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A breach notification procedure that names the applicable reporting obligations and their deadlines, assigns responsible parties, defines timelines and notice content, and, where a breach occurred, notification records showing affected parties and regulators were notified within the required window.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A one-line statement that the company will notify affected users, with no named regulatory obligations, no timelines, and no responsible parties.
red_flags: No specific statutory deadlines are identified, such as a 72 hour regulator window or state notification laws
No named responsible party or role owns the notification
Contractual customer notification commitments are not reflected in the procedure
A breach occurred during the period but no notification record exists, or notice was sent late with no explanation
The procedure is generic and does not reference the entity's actual regulators or customer contracts

platform_hints.notion: The breach procedure often lives in the incident response or security policy space, and notification records may be tracked as incident pages.
platform_hints.google_workspace: Notifications to affected users or regulators are usually sent emails; pull the sent messages with timestamps as the record.

PRI-08.title: Data Subject Accounting Requests
PRI-08.description: {company_name} maintains an inventory of personal information types and handling processes, and responds to data controller or data subject accounting requests, providing information about what personal data is held and to whom it has been disclosed.
PRI-08.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization respond to requests from individuals asking for an accounting of how their data has been disclosed? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data subject accounting requests practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Can you provide data subjects with an accounting of how their personal information has been disclosed?
follow_ups: Do you maintain records of disclosures?
How do data subjects request this information?

evidence_goals: Pull the records of processing activities or data inventory listing personal information types, handling processes, and the third parties data is disclosed to
Pull the documented procedure for responding to accounting requests about what personal data is held and to whom it has been disclosed
For any accounting requests during the period, pull the tracking records showing receipt date, response date, and the information provided, or obtain confirmation that none occurred
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A maintained data inventory or records of processing activities that maps personal information types to processes and named third-party recipients, a written procedure for handling accounting requests with a response timeframe, and, where requests occurred, tracking records showing each was answered within that timeframe.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A statement that the company would answer such a request, with no data inventory of disclosures and no procedure or intake channel.
red_flags: No data inventory or records of processing activities exist, so disclosures cannot actually be reconstructed
Third-party recipients are not recorded, making an accounting impossible
No defined intake channel or response timeframe for requests
Requests were received but not logged, or were answered outside the stated timeframe
The data inventory is stale and does not reflect current subprocessors or integrations

platform_hints.notion: The records of processing activities and subprocessor list are commonly Notion pages or a linked spreadsheet, and requests may be tracked as a table.
platform_hints.linear: Accounting or data requests may be tracked as issues; check receipt and resolution timestamps.

PRI-09.title: Data Quality
PRI-09.description: {company_name} keeps personal information accurate, complete, and relevant to its stated purposes, using validation at collection and self-service updates, with periodic reviews removing data no longer needed.
PRI-09.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization maintain the accuracy of personal information it holds? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have data quality practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you ensure the quality and accuracy of personal information you maintain?
follow_ups: Are there processes for data subjects to correct inaccurate data?
How do you prevent use of inaccurate data?

evidence_goals: Pull the data quality controls documentation showing validation applied at collection and the self-service capability for data subjects to view and correct their own information
Pull dated records of periodic data relevance or retention reviews showing that personal information no longer needed for the stated purposes is identified and removed
Pull a walkthrough or screenshot of the product path where a data subject updates or corrects their own information
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: Documentation of validation at collection plus a working self-service update path for data subjects, backed by dated records of periodic reviews that identified and removed personal information no longer relevant to the stated purposes.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A claim that data is kept accurate with no evidence of validation rules, no user-facing correction path, and no record that any relevance or retention review actually happened.
red_flags: No validation at collection, so any value is accepted for emails, identifiers, or key fields
Data subjects cannot view or correct their own information
No periodic review has occurred, so stale or irrelevant data is never removed
Retention or minimization is described in policy but has no execution records
Reviews are claimed but undated and unassigned to anyone

platform_hints.notion: Data quality or retention review records and their dates often live as Notion pages or a review log.
platform_hints.google_workspace: Periodic review notes or a retention checklist may be kept as a Doc or Sheet with edit history showing when the review ran.

PRI-10.title: Privacy Monitoring & Dispute Resolution
PRI-10.description: {company_name} publishes a privacy contact and runs a documented process to receive, investigate, and resolve privacy inquiries, complaints, and disputes. Compliance is monitored on an ongoing basis, with noncompliance documented and corrected.
PRI-10.na_trigger: Is the Privacy TSC category in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization monitor its privacy practices and handle complaints or disputes about personal information? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have privacy monitoring and dispute resolution practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you monitor your privacy practices and handle privacy-related complaints or disputes?
follow_ups: Do you have a privacy monitoring program?
How are complaints handled?
Are privacy incidents tracked and resolved?

evidence_goals: Pull the published contact channel for privacy inquiries and complaints, such as a privacy email or form on the site or in the notice
Pull the documented complaint handling procedure covering intake, investigation, resolution, and communication, including response timeframes
Pull the ongoing privacy monitoring records and any noncompliance register showing issues found, reported, and corrected
For any privacy disputes during the period, pull the resolution records showing investigation, outcome, and the communication sent to the data subject
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A published privacy contact channel, a written complaint handling procedure with response timeframes, dated monitoring records and a noncompliance register with corrective actions, and, where disputes occurred, records showing each was investigated, resolved, and communicated to the data subject.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A privacy email address on the site with no procedure behind it, no monitoring records, and no evidence that any complaint or noncompliance was ever tracked.
red_flags: No published privacy contact channel, or it routes to a generic support inbox with no privacy handling
The complaint procedure has no response timeframe or no investigation step
No ongoing monitoring records exist, so compliance is assumed rather than checked
Noncompliance instances are not logged or have no corrective actions recorded
Disputes were received but resolutions were never documented or communicated back to the data subject

platform_hints.google_workspace: The privacy inbox and complaint correspondence live in Gmail; pull threads showing intake, investigation, and the response sent.
platform_hints.notion: The complaint handling procedure, monitoring records, and the noncompliance register are commonly Notion pages or tables.

AI-01.title: AI Provider Inventory & Data-Use Terms
AI-01.description: {company_name} inventories the hosted AI model providers that process entity or customer data and governs each like a subprocessor: a written agreement on file, training and data-use terms identified, and providers receiving customer data disclosed in the subprocessor list.
AI-01.na_trigger: Applies only when hosted AI model providers process entity or customer data

collection.gating_question: Does your organization send any data to hosted AI model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar model APIs? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have AI provider inventory and data use practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Which hosted AI model providers process your entity or customer data, and how are they inventoried and governed?
follow_ups: Which hosted AI model providers do you send data to, and what data does each one receive?
Do you have a signed agreement or data processing addendum with each provider?
Have you identified whether each provider uses your data to train its models?
Do the providers that receive customer data appear on your subprocessor list?

evidence_commands.shows: Lists the hosted AI provider SDKs the application actually depends on, so the reviewer can reconcile the provider inventory against the providers the codebase integrates and catch any provider that is in use but missing from the inventory.
Lists stored API credentials so AI provider keys can be reconciled against the provider inventory, surfacing any provider whose credentials are held but which is not recorded in the inventory.

evidence_goals: Obtain the inventory of hosted AI model providers with the data each one receives and the sending system
Obtain the signed agreement or data processing addendum for each provider that handles customer data
Obtain the customer subprocessor list and reconcile it against the providers that receive customer data
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A per provider inventory naming each hosted model provider, the categories of data it receives, and the system or feature that sends the data, with a signed agreement or data processing addendum on file for each provider that handles customer data, model training and retention terms identified per provider, and every provider that receives customer data listed on the subprocessor list.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A general statement that AI providers are trusted or compliant with no per provider list. Model training terms asserted verbally or copied from a provider marketing page. Providers present in the codebase or credential store but absent from the inventory.
red_flags: Hosted AI provider integrated in the codebase but missing from the inventory
Customer data sent to a provider that has no signed agreement or data processing addendum
Model training or retention terms not identified for a provider
Provider receiving customer data absent from the subprocessor list
Free tier or personal provider accounts used to process customer data

platform_hints.github: Search the dependency manifests and application config for AI provider SDKs and base URLs to establish the true set of providers in use, then reconcile against the inventory.
platform_hints.openai: The provider inventory entry should record whether the OpenAI account is a business account and reference the applicable terms and data processing addendum that govern API data.
platform_hints.anthropic: Record the Anthropic commercial terms and any data processing addendum, and note the default posture that inputs and outputs submitted through the API are not used to train models.

AI-02.title: Model Provider Data-Use Configuration
AI-02.description: {company_name} verifies that organization-level settings at each hosted AI provider prevent submitted inputs and outputs from training the provider's models, with retention windows set to the defined period, including zero-data-retention arrangements where in effect.
AI-02.na_trigger: Applies only when hosted AI model providers process entity or customer data

collection.gating_question: Have you configured your accounts at your AI model providers to control whether your data is used for training and how long it is retained? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have AI provider data use configuration practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How have you configured your AI model provider accounts to control training on your data and data retention?
follow_ups: Where in each provider's console is the setting that controls training on your data?
What retention window is configured at each provider, or do you have a zero data retention arrangement?
Does the setting apply to every project, workspace, or API key under your organization account?

evidence_commands.shows: Enumerates every project under the OpenAI organization. Because the training and retention data controls are set at the organization level, this lets the reviewer confirm the setting covers all active projects rather than a single one. Look for any project not expected to be in scope.

Lists every Anthropic workspace under the organization so the reviewer can confirm the organization no training posture and any retention arrangement apply to all workspaces in use. Look for unexpected or personal workspaces.

evidence_goals: Capture, from the entity's own provider account, the setting that controls whether submitted data is used to train the provider's models
Capture the configured retention window from the entity's own provider account, or the signed zero data retention arrangement
Enumerate all projects, workspaces, or API keys under the organization to confirm the organization level setting covers every one
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A console screenshot or export from the entity's own provider account showing training on submitted data disabled and the retention window set to the entity's defined period, or a signed zero data retention addendum, plus an enumeration of all projects or workspaces confirming the setting applies organization wide.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A provider marketing page or default policy statement offered as proof of this organization's configuration. A screenshot of one project or key while other active projects remain uncovered. A verbal claim that training is off with nothing pulled from the account.
red_flags: No training posture supported only by the provider's public policy page rather than the entity's own account settings
Setting shown for one project or key while other active projects or workspaces are not covered
Retention left at a longer default than the entity's defined period with no justification
Personal or free tier provider account processing entity or customer data
Zero data retention claimed but no signed arrangement on file

platform_hints.openai: The setting that disables training on API data lives under Settings then Data Controls in the OpenAI dashboard. Capture that panel from the entity's own organization. Use the Admin API projects endpoint to enumerate the projects the organization level setting covers. API data is not used to train models by default, but capture the account setting rather than citing the policy page.
platform_hints.anthropic: Anthropic does not train on inputs or outputs submitted through the API by default. Where the entity relies on this, capture the account or workspace confirmation and any signed zero data retention or no training addendum. Use the Admin API workspaces endpoint to enumerate workspaces.
platform_hints.azure: Azure OpenAI does not use prompts or completions to train models and by default stores prompts up to 30 days for abuse monitoring, which can be waived through an approved modified abuse monitoring form. Capture the resource configuration and any approved waiver.

AI-03.title: Customer Data Boundaries for AI Features
AI-03.description: {company_name} defines which data categories may be sent to hosted AI provider APIs and enforces that boundary through a technical control such as redaction or an allowlist. Submitted data is not used to train provider models, and any training on customer data requires documented authorization.
AI-03.na_trigger: Applies only when hosted AI model providers process entity or customer data

collection.gating_question: Does your product send data to hosted AI model provider APIs such as OpenAI or Anthropic? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have defined customer data boundaries for AI features in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: What data does your product send to hosted AI model providers, and how do you keep excluded data out of those calls?
follow_ups: Which categories of data are never sent to model providers, and where is that written down?
How is that boundary enforced in the code path before a call reaches the provider?
Are your provider accounts or contracts set so submitted data is not used to train their models?
Do you fine-tune or train any model on customer data, and if so how is that authorized?
documents: AI Model Provider Configuration (OpenAI / Anthropic / Azure OpenAI)

evidence_commands.command: gh search code --owner {org} 'redact OR sanitize openai anthropic'
evidence_commands.shows: Locates the code that redacts or allowlists fields before payloads reach the model provider client. Look for a sanitizer or allowlist wrapping the provider SDK call, and confirm excluded categories cannot pass through.

evidence_commands.command: gh api -X GET search/code -f q='openai OR anthropic org:{org} language:python' --jq '.items[].path'
evidence_commands.shows: Lists every file that references the model provider SDKs so you can confirm all provider calls route through the boundary or redaction layer and none bypass it.

Lists configured AI Gateways. If the entity routes provider calls through an AI Gateway, look for the logging and data control settings that enforce the boundary. Absent if the entity calls providers directly.
Lists fine-tuning jobs and their training files. Confirms whether the entity fine-tunes models and, if so, what data was used, which must reconcile to authorization records.

evidence_goals: Obtain the written rule naming which data categories may and may not be sent to hosted model providers
Obtain source code or gateway configuration showing the redaction or allowlist enforced before provider calls
Obtain provider account data-control settings or executed agreements showing submitted data is excluded from training
Obtain the list of fine-tuning or training runs and, where customer data was used, the authorization on file
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A dated rule listing allowed and excluded categories, code showing an enforced redaction or allowlist on the single path to the provider client, provider settings or a signed agreement excluding submitted data from training, and either no customer-data training or an authorization record per run.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A general statement that sensitive data is not sent, with no rule and no enforcement in code. Provider defaults assumed rather than shown. A client-authored spreadsheet asserting configuration state.
red_flags: Secrets, full payment card numbers, or regulated personal data reaching provider payloads
A redaction function that exists in code but is bypassed on some provider call paths
Reliance on a consumer chat plan setting as evidence for API data handling
Fine-tuning jobs on customer data with no authorization on file

platform_hints.openai: Check organization data controls for training on API data. List fine-tuning jobs and their training files. Confirm the account, not a consumer plan, is what production uses.
platform_hints.anthropic: Confirm API usage is covered by terms that exclude submitted data from training, and check for an executed commercial agreement or zero-retention arrangement where applicable.
platform_hints.github: Search for the provider SDK usage and the redaction or allowlist wrapper. Confirm every call site routes through it.
platform_hints.cloudflare: If an AI Gateway fronts provider calls, pull its logging and data control settings and confirm all traffic is routed through it.
platform_hints.azure: For Azure OpenAI, confirm the deployment and content filtering configuration and that submitted data is not used to train foundation models per the service terms.

AI-04.title: AI Interaction Logging & Retention
AI-04.description: {company_name} inventories where prompt and completion logs are stored, including logs held by LLM observability tools, applies a defined retention period to those logs, restricts access to them, and either redacts sensitive data in the logs or documents the retained exposure.
AI-04.na_trigger: Applies only when hosted AI model providers process entity or customer data

collection.gating_question: Do you store the prompts and responses from your AI features, including in tools like Langfuse, Helicone, or Datadog? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have AI interaction logging and retention practices in place. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: Where are your AI prompts and responses logged, how long are they kept, and who can read them?
follow_ups: Which systems hold prompt and completion logs, including any observability tool?
What retention is set on those logs, and how is it enforced?
Who has access to the logs, and is sensitive data redacted before it is stored?

evidence_commands.shows: Confirms prompt and completion traces are captured in the observability tool. Inspect the returned fields to see what prompt and response content is retained and whether it is redacted.
Lists log indexes and their retention in days. Confirms the retention actually enforced on AI logs sent to Datadog matches the stated period.

evidence_commands.command: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT jobname, schedule, command FROM cron.job;"
evidence_commands.shows: Lists scheduled jobs. Look for a purge or deletion job on the prompt and completion log table that enforces retention for self-stored logs. Absent if no such job runs.
Shows the schema of the self-stored AI log table including a timestamp column needed to enforce retention and which columns hold prompt and completion content. The table name will vary by entity.

evidence_goals: Obtain the inventory of every store holding prompt and completion logs, including observability tools
Obtain the retention configuration or purge jobs enforcing deletion of AI logs after the defined period
Obtain the access configuration on each log store and evidence of redaction or a documented exposure decision
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A current inventory covering application databases, observability tools, and accessible provider logs, retention visibly configured on each store, access limited to named roles, and sampled log entries showing redaction or a documented acceptance of what remains.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: A statement that logs are kept safely without naming the stores. A stated retention with no enforcing setting or job. Broad access to raw prompt and completion content. A client-authored spreadsheet asserting retention or access state.
red_flags: An observability tool in active use that is missing from the inventory
Prompt and completion logs retained indefinitely with no retention configured
Raw customer prompts containing sensitive data readable by all staff
Redaction claimed in policy but visible sensitive data in a sampled log entry

platform_hints.langfuse: Pull traces to confirm capture and inspect retained fields. Check project members for access scope and any data masking settings.
platform_hints.datadog: Pull log index retention. Confirm sensitive attributes are excluded or scrubbed via pipelines, and restrict who can query the AI log index.
platform_hints.postgres: For self-stored logs, pull the table schema and any pg_cron purge job enforcing retention. Confirm role grants limit access.
platform_hints.helicone: Confirm request and response logging scope, retention setting, and member access. Check whether omission or redaction of sensitive fields is enabled.
platform_hints.supabase: Check the log table schema, row level security or role grants restricting access, and a scheduled job enforcing retention.

HIP-01.title: Business Associate Agreements
HIP-01.description: {company_name} executes business associate agreements before electronic protected health information is created, received, maintained, or transmitted on its behalf or on behalf of a customer, and with every subcontractor that handles ePHI. Agreements include the content required by 45 CFR 164.314(a), including security incident reporting and subcontractor flow-down.
HIP-01.na_trigger: Is the HIPAA compliance add-on in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization sign business associate agreements (BAAs) with the customers and vendors that handle protected health information? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not execute business associate agreements for its ePHI relationships. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How do you manage business associate agreements with the customers and subcontractors that touch ePHI?
follow_ups: Which customers and vendors create, receive, store, or transmit ePHI with you?
Do you have a BAA in place with your cloud infrastructure provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure)?
Do you sign BAAs with every subcontractor that can access ePHI?
Does your BAA cover security incident reporting and flow-down of the same obligations to subcontractors?

evidence_goals: Pull the inventory or data flow document identifying which customers and subcontractors handle ePHI
Pull executed BAAs for customer relationships involving ePHI, with signature dates
Pull executed downstream BAAs for subcontractors that handle ePHI, including the cloud provider BAA
Pull the BAA template or a representative executed agreement showing the required terms
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A vendor or customer inventory that flags every ePHI counterparty, a signed BAA on file for each of them (the cloud provider's console-accepted BAA counts), and operative terms that require Security Rule compliance, subcontractor flow-down, and security incident reporting.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: ePHI flowing to customers or vendors with no inventory of who those parties are, sampled relationships with no executed agreement to show, or a BAA that omits one of the required elements.
red_flags: No identification of which counterparties handle ePHI
A customer relationship where ePHI handling began before any BAA was signed, with no documented interim arrangement carrying the required terms for that window
A subcontractor with access to ePHI excluded from BAA scope without a documented rationale
BAA terms silent on subcontractor flow-down or on incident reporting

platform_hints.google_drive: Pull the executed BAA folder and the vendor inventory spreadsheet. Check the ePHI flag column against the data flow document.
platform_hints.notion: Pull the vendor register page and any BAA tracker. Executed agreements usually live as attachments or links on each vendor's page.
platform_hints.aws: The AWS BAA is accepted through AWS Artifact. Pull the Artifact agreement acceptance page showing the account and acceptance date.

HIP-02.title: Emergency Access Procedure
HIP-02.description: {company_name} maintains a documented emergency access procedure for obtaining access to systems containing electronic protected health information when normal access paths are unavailable. Emergency credentials are restricted and secured, and any use is logged and reviewed afterward.
HIP-02.na_trigger: Is the HIPAA compliance add-on in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization have a documented way to reach systems containing ePHI when normal sign-in paths are down (a break-glass procedure)? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not have a documented emergency access procedure for systems containing ePHI. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How would your team get into production systems holding ePHI if the normal sign-in path (SSO or your identity provider) were unavailable?
follow_ups: Where are the break-glass credentials stored, and who can reach them?
What circumstances qualify as an emergency, and who is authorized to invoke the procedure?
Is use of the emergency path logged, and is any use reviewed afterward?

evidence_commands.shows: Whether the root break-glass identity has MFA enabled and whether standing root access keys exist

evidence_goals: Pull the documented emergency access procedure covering qualifying circumstances, authorized personnel, and the steps to obtain access
Pull the inventory of emergency access paths (break-glass accounts, root credentials, recovery codes) and where each is secured
Pull the access log for the break-glass identity over the period, and the post-use review record for any use
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A written break-glass section naming who may invoke emergency access and when, credentials enumerated and locked to those people (a restricted vault entry or a physically secured device), and a log showing either zero uses or uses that each carry an after-the-fact review.
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Emergency access that exists only as tribal knowledge, a root password sitting in a vault the whole team can read, or an emergency sign-in during the period that nobody went back and reviewed.
red_flags: No written procedure, or a procedure that names no authorized personnel
Emergency credentials reachable by people outside the named set
Root or break-glass sign-ins with no post-use review on record
No logging on the emergency path at all

platform_hints.aws: Pull the account summary showing root MFA, and CloudTrail sign-in events filtered to the root identity for the period.
platform_hints.1password: Pull the vault access report for the break-glass vault showing which people can reach the entry.
platform_hints.gcp: Pull the organization admin sign-in audit log filtered to the recovery or super-admin identity.

HIP-03.title: Security Documentation Retention
HIP-03.description: {company_name} retains its security policies and the records of required security activities, including risk assessments, access reviews, incident documentation, and training records, for at least six years from creation or the date last in effect, whichever is later, and can retrieve historical versions.
HIP-03.na_trigger: Is the HIPAA compliance add-on in scope for this engagement?

collection.gating_question: Does your organization keep security policies and security activity records (risk assessments, reviews, incident notes, training records) for a defined retention period? (Yes/No)
collection.absent_reason_template: Entity does not define retention for security policies and security activity records. All attributes for this control marked absent. This is a structural gap requiring implementation.
collection.question: How long do you keep security policies and the records of security activities, and can you still open an old version of a policy?
follow_ups: Is there a written retention requirement covering security documentation, and does it reach six years?
Where do records of risk assessments, access reviews, incidents, and training live?
Can you retrieve an earlier version of a policy (version history, archive folder, or a system that preserves prior versions)?
documents: Retention schedule or policy governance section

evidence_goals: Pull the written retention requirement covering security policies and security activity records, showing the six year floor
Pull proof that historical versions are retrievable: version history on the policy repository, an archive folder, or retention settings on the system of record
collection_playbook.what_good_looks_like: A retention statement that names security policies and activity records with a period of at least six years, and a repository that demonstrably produces prior versions (open an old version live, or show the archive).
collection_playbook.what_bad_looks_like: Retention defined only for customer data or logs while security documentation goes unmentioned, or policies edited in place in a tool whose history window cannot reach back to earlier versions.
red_flags: No retention requirement for security documentation anywhere in the policy suite
A stated period shorter than six years
Policies edited in place with version history disabled or time-limited
Security activity records (reviews, incidents, training) with no defined home

platform_hints.google_drive: Open version history on the security policy and show the oldest available version. Pull the shared drive's archive folder listing if one exists.
platform_hints.notion: Page history depth depends on the plan. Pull the workspace plan settings alongside the page history so the retention window is verifiable.
platform_hints.github: Policies kept in a repo carry full history. Pull the file's commit log showing the earliest versions.
